<@profile.key>Everyone called her "Younger Dame" at Qingbo Stockade because Ruan Lin had only one child of his own, and later plucked another out of the water. The first was named "One (Yi)," so the second naturally became "Younger". The folks of Qingbo Stockade always thought in simple, straightforward ways.
No one knew where Younger Dame came from. Ruan Yi said she was a kitten in a bamboo basket that he picked up. Ruan Lin said she was a treasure, the River's Daughter sent by the Ancestral Spring. A young boy nearby, hearing this, asked, if Younger Dame was born of the river, didn't that make her the river's master?! Upon hearing this, Tangtang puffed out her chest, leaped onto her bamboo hobbyhorse, and declared proudly: "Exactly! The water is mine! Qingbo Stockade is mine! All the good food and fun are mine too!"
Ruan Lin ruffled her hair and burst into hearty laughter. Soon, everyone gathered around the fire joined in, their mirth contagious enough to make Tangtang giggle along. The conversation drifted to other things, and the matter was never brought up again.
It wasn't until Tangtang grew a little older that one day, as she listened to the Stockaders talking, a thought suddenly struck her. River water couldn't give birth to a Feline like her. Where were her real parents?
Tangtang couldn't make sense of it. She spent days comparing herself to everyone in the Stockade. Some were too sturdy, others too short. Not a single one had ears or a tail as beautiful as hers.
This dilemma weighed on Tangtang for quite some time, until Ruan Lin called her over for ironpot stewed fin. Tangtang glanced at Ruan Yi's bowl, then at her own. The head, eyes, and tender belly of the fin were all in hers. As she picked out the fin belly and stuffed it into Ruan Lin's mouth, she thought to herself: "Why should I care about what the Stockaders yammer about 'mommy's touch'? Dad's cooking is delish and that's enough for me!"

After extensive investigation and verification, the HR Division confirmed that Tangtang was still an unweaned babe when she was found. Given the physiologies of a newborn, it would have been impossible for her to drift far along the river. Therefore, it is preliminarily inferred that she was abandoned somewhere close to Qingbo Stockade.
After conducting detailed examinations and evaluations of her eye, Medical Division personnel suspect that the pattern within it is closely linked to her Originium Arts. Given the pattern's high degree of regularity, it can be ruled out as a random symptom arising from Oripathy infection. Instead, it is more likely related to her familial medical history. However, after reviewing all preserved personnel records of Qingbo Stockade, no individuals with similar conditions to hers were found.
To quote her own account: "I just practiced and practiced by the water, and this pattern appeared by itself."
This is absolutely impossible. We sought assistance from HAS, and after reviewing resident archives, they were likewise unable to identify Tangtang's relatives. However, a Tianshi specializing in Yan history made a breakthrough: within the Yan documents passed down from Terra, she discovered records highly relevant to the pattern in Tangtang's eye. According to legendary accounts in the literature, this pattern symbolizes the evolution of heaven and earth, containing ancient knowledge inheritance. Yet Tangtang clearly lacks access to such learning. The Tianshi of Wuling were equally astonished by this discovery. They had never imagined that such a unique user of Originium Arts existed right within their reach.
In conclusion, the specific reasons behind Tangtang's abandonment in Qingbo Stockade ... may be more complex than we initially assumed.
...
After we shared the investigation findings with Tangtang, she simply scratched her head and said her origins weren't all that important. After all, she had family and friends now, living a good life. Though she did wonder, just a little, if she still has blood relatives, and how they might be faring ... She emphasized it was just a little, about the size of a small shellbeast's claw.
Tangtang still keeps the small swaddling cloth she was wrapped in back then. When handing the fabric over to us, she noticeably hesitated for a moment before returning to her usual carefree demeanor: "And remember to give it back once you're done checking!"</>

-678466429771217550:
"Sir Huang, the SAR teams we dispatched this morning have returned. None of them found any of the scientists on the list. We haven't heard anything from the team that went out this afternoon." 
"Hmm. Stay vigilant. Are the wounded getting proper treatment?" 
"We acted according to your instructions. Those with light injuries have been housed at a temporary shelter. The critically injured have been medevaced to the nearest city for more extensive treatment." 
The old man sighed. Seventy-two hours had passed since the search and rescue (SAR) teams arrived at Wuling. And for seventy-two hours, the area around Wuling Science Station had remained submerged in the Blight Tide. HAS had invested its entire SAR capacity but failed to extricate any of the scientists trapped within the facility. 
After receiving the orders, the young watchguard in his PPE overalls saluted and headed out. None of them had slept ever since the tent that served as their temporary HQ was pitched. 
Peace returned to the command post. The only ones left in the tent were the old man and his disciples who were busy monitoring the status of the Very Large Rift. 
"Tianshi Huang," a messenger bearing the latest orders from the Headquarters arrived. 
"Appreciate the special delivery. I've received the documents. With Endfield's help, full restoration of long-range comms will be achieved by tomorrow morning. Messenger, I pray you can deliver this message to the temporary comm station outside Wuling and notify HQ of this update ASAP." 
"It will be done. And we appreciate your hard work." 
"Any instructions from the Academy?" the nearby Tianshi gathered around Huang after the messenger left. However, their faces froze when they read the contents of the document. 
"After twenty-four hours, Hongshan Headquarters shall ... vote on whether we should suspend SAR operations in the rift rupture zone. The HQ believes that the opinions of the site personnel are extremely important." 
"Vote? Why? Rupture growth has slowed down for now! It's obvious!" 
"Maybe their next move would be asking us to bring everyone back to HQ." 
"Are we giving up the entire region of Wuling?" 
After a brief moment of silence, the old Tianshi arranged the work for various SAR teams. 
"Keep your ideas to yourself. Other orders might come in once long-range comms are restored tomorrow. I'm taking the night shift. Use the opportunity to rest." 
"Understood. Then let's ... excuse ourselves for now." 
"Good luck, sir." 
Silence returned to the tent. The old man stood before the map hologram as the blinking red lights reflected off his eyes and glowed against the wrinkled piece of paper he held. 
His daughter as well as his own disciples were still there. 
The old man gritted his teeth. With shaking hands he held up the monitoring reports his disciples left at the HQ and studied them under the lamplight. The inexperienced youths did not know that the cessation of rupture expansion did not translate into the containment of the threat. Instead, it was a herald to a greater disaster waiting to happen. All Blight matter near the rift would slowly "accumulate" and a secondary rupture would suddenly burst forth during this false lull of safety. He had noticed this phenomenon before he celebrated his thirtieth birthday, while he was a strong young man of adventure, courage, and energy. 
The old man sat down on a plastic chair. For the first time in his life, he felt the need for retirement. 

"Dozens of hours have passed. Unfortunately, we have picked up no vital signs in the vicinity of the Very Large Rift. Since we have a unanimous consensus, we shall act upon the decision and cease all SAR operations—" 
The receiver was placed before the old Tianshi. The HQ had voted. His work was to announce their final decision. 
The young Tianshi leaped to their feet and roared at him. The youths stood their ground and argued for another round of SAR operations. 
He remembered saying something else and how he reiterated the importance of the decision. 
But in the end, the old man closed his eyes and spoke no more.

It was early autumn and already the snow was falling in the north of Talos-II. Beneath the heavy gray skies, snowflakes fell as bone-chilling winds howled across the plains, unchallenged by the wilting grass as it burrowed into an old, leaking observation post... There the winds were briefly checked by a campfire before they stopped by a young man's cheek.
"ACHOO!"
The sneezing did not slow the young Perro speed in stuffing two slabs of bread and a meat stew into his mouth. He even wanted to lick the plate if he could.
"Oh... Thanks a lot for this..."
"You're welcome. The cold drove us to this campfire. We're friends now."
The grinning Forte "chef" sat by the campfire and gazed at him. He looked around thirty or so.
"So, friend, why venture to the North alone?"
"I'm trying to visit the masters of the fighting arts and complete my Catalog of Warriors Under the Heavens! Oh, that's just a book with the backstories of every warrior... We have this legendary master named Chen Chichi of Hongshan but nobody knew where she went. I thought I could visit the North and find out... But as luck would have it, the Aggeloi was the one that chased me all the way here. Dammit, I bet we'd be getting another Ankhorfall soon enough."
The Forte helped himself to a ladle of the stew.
"I know this one. Orphaned at a young age and got admitted to Tanjian Hall where she became the worst disciple of the cohort. But after doing her Jianghu tours, she became a legend amongst those of her generation and a lauded master of swordmancy... Even got herself a happy family. Husband's quite the master in leapmancy. They also have a daughter. Name's Chen Qianyu, I think."
"That's so detailed. Are you a swordmancer as well?"
"I learned a few swordmancy moves from the wildlands from a Songseeker."
"So, what do you think about Master Chen Chichi?"
"A great and imposing mountain."
"Yeah... She's the dream of every swordmancer. They say her swordmancy is imbued with a state of unrestrained freedom. It's more than being faster than a comet. Those who witnessed her sword singing across the skies could feel the 'heavens and earth' itself. It felt as though everything in this world, from the tallest peaks to the deepest seas, has achieved oneness with her blade. Her sword itself is light and elegant. It's like a speck of dust and a gust of wind. It strikes with a force contained within every existence... I can hardly imagine anything that could withstand her blade. Not even the Aggelos..."
"Ankhor."
"Indeed. Her sword can probably cleave the largest Ankhors in two..."
"I'm saying we have an Ankhorfall."
The young Perro instantly leaped up without raising his head, jumped over the campfire, and bounded for the outside.
"You can't outrun an Ankhor."
"Well, at least I won't be crushed by it. I'll take my luck outrunning its Aggeloid spawn."
"Haha. That'd be quite a challenge. We lost that race years ago."
The Forte strolled out casually and slowly.
"When I was a lad, I herded stockbeasts for a Songseeker. We were surrounded by the Aggeloi when a swordmancer drew her iron blade and unleashed a crimson cleave that pulverized the rock buggers. A master leapmancer then grabbed me with his arms and helped me escape the encirclement... I spent years traveling and paid more than a few visits to Hongshan, but my search has found nothing. I have nothing but respect for this couple..."
The Forte then drew swords from his hip scabbards.
"I may not achieve their levels of mastery, but such is my goal. I spent years honing my swordmancy and managed to replicate a fraction of that overwhelming cleave I have witnessed. This is one auspicious day. May you witness my achievement."
The Ankhor smote the ground and turned their former shelter to a pile of rubble.
What followed was a flurry of glinting blades.

The Ætherside has always been influencing our lives. Is there anyone else who knows more about the Ætherside than us? Probably not... Wait, no... I think they do exist, the Endfielders ... those working in the best labs of the TGCC and UWST ... and the strange ones who roam the wilderness but have a knack for it. They also have great knowledge for the Ætherside too. 
This is why I am confused, dear. My inability to find you made me realize that I hardly know anything about the Ætherside. Nothing living should exist there. I shouldn't be feeling you at all, but the gentle sensations emanating from the stump where you were severed felt so clear and real. Part of my mind is fighting another. The conclusion has caused the corpus of my knowledge, one that I have meticulously constructed over the years, to utterly collapse. 
I think I need to head out a little. 
...... 
They have begun to inject me with sedatives. 
...... 
I went looking for a former classmate. We grew up and studied together, and spent many years trying to one-up each other in our work and the impact factor of our research projects. He was shocked at the shallow and obvious nature of my question... I only asked him for his views on the Ætherside. Instead, he answered my question with another question: How do I regard the rising of the sun and the falling of the moon? Or the four seasons? I told him I am part of the seasonal cycle, and part of me rests in the rising sun and falling moon. 
He then called the police. The public safety officers of La Fantoma arrived quickly. 
...... 
I believe I have arrived at a UWST auto-farm. Convincing the ex-Oathkeeper security guard that I am not a Landbreaker in disguise proved quite a challenge. He shared some food and we sat before a stove, toasting with our good right hands. I asked him the same question. Fury, hatred, and a sprinkle of cowardice came to his eyes. He emptied his cup and then told me a story he heard when he was a boy. It was a tale about killing the ocean. 
The fire burned in his chest. I cannot let this fire harm you. Fortunately, I carried some sleeping pills with me. 
...... 
I can feel you very clearly now. 
...... 
The Archosauria woman sat within a formation of denstacks. Hah. She thinks her performance is impressive, but I saw right through her. I've used you to flip through numerous tomes to read about the conquerors and sovereigns whose names were noted down by history... I know the lies spat out by her kind of people. Listen to her voice, the empty shells of promises she sugarcoats. She treats the Ætherside as a tool... Of course, I might've been seeing things due to my extreme hunger. Anyway, if her theatrics and performance deceive me, then she's really good at what she's doing. 
...... 
I can wait no longer. I am going to find you. That Lei Fa thunder-casting Tianshi has not noticed me as I infiltrated the Exclusion Zone... I should be able to find a passage that leads to your location. 
...... 
The colors are so beautiful. I must enter it. It's time to go ... and become one with it.

<@profile.key>Mr. Dolly's Game III 
Gazing out at the glistening coastline and distant skyscrapers, a long-forgotten name came to Ardelia's mind — Siesta, a volcanic city wrapped in warm memories. 
But, this was La Fantoma — the gem of Band, the gilded city of Talos-II. 
As a renowned geologist, Ardelia was invited to speak at a major academic forum on "Order in the New Geological Ecology of Talos-II." She had only planned to deliver a standard presentation, but to her surprise, her speech caused quite a stir. 
Corporate representatives quickly surrounded her, sharing blueprints for a new industrial park and asking for her thoughts. Senior researchers eagerly shared their latest findings, hoping to spark potential collaborations with Ardelia. Even government officials brought thick binders and invited her to join their next major project. 
Just like that, a quiet field researcher had become the star of the show. 
What began as simple handshakes soon turned into warm compliments — "You're an inspiration to us all." In the elevator, someone stopped Ardelia with a notebook, asking for an autograph to hang in his lab. At crosswalks, kids would shout, "I wanna be a scientist too!" Even a street vendor handed her a soda, saying, "My nephew loves geology — got any book recommendations?" 
At first, Ardelia found it moving. She nodded politely to every earnest face, patiently answered each well-meaning question. But slowly, exhaustion crept in. She didn't resent these people, nor did she dislike their attention. It was just… she wasn't ready to be "known". 
After a grueling three-hour roundtable, she pushed open the door and ran. She passed a giant poster of herself labeled "Young Female Scientist Role Model" and vanished into the crowd. 
That's when she realized: Mr. Dolly was gone. 
No one knew what it was or where it had gone. In a shopping mall, a woman screamed about "something fluffy" bumping into her. On a rooftop, a flower bed was trampled flat by "something pink." Someone even posted a blurry photo "something round" darting over the ticket gate — carrying a bag of cotton candy. 
Ardelia tracked these clues and searched half of the city. Her shoes wore thin, mud clung to her skirt, and headache crept over her. 
Nearly out of breath, she stumbled out of a side alley and stopped. 
It was a patch of untouched wilderness at the city's edge — untamed, bursting with wildflowers. The sea breeze carried their fragrance in gentle waves. And there, lay Mr. Dolly, sprawled at the heart of it all, motionless as the earth itself. 
"What are you even doing here?" Ardelia asked, half-frustrated, half-amused. Mr. Dolly didn't answer. He just rolled over lazily. 
Ardelia walked over and sat beside him. Then, she switched off her handyterm. The meetings, the obligations — all of it could wait. 
After all, nothing suits a geologist better than the open wild. </>

<@profile.key>The hinge of the courtyard gate had broken down for a while. It probably broke two weeks after Chen Chichi left. When Guang Jianshan noticed the hinge broken in two, he couldn't help but feel he had already seen this coming. Every time someone pushed open the gate to enter or leave the garden, the hinge would release an irksome groan loud enough to be heard in the house. Even the study. The groan at five during sunrise was Chen heading out to practice swordmancy. The groan at eight in the morning was Chen rushing back home, picking up her school bag, grabbing the food from her father's plate, taking two messy bites out of it, and rushing out to Tanjian Hall for her classes. The groan at five in the afternoon was Chen running back into the courtyard while chasing fowlbeasts through the grove, humming a song, and swishing a well-balanced stick around. The groan at midnight was Chen secretly jumping out of her second floor bedroom. She thought her father would not know how she sneaked off to have fun on her own. 
Jianshan knew everything. He had quietly paved a flat path leading to the gate and got rid of the protruding stones. He would not want his careless darling girl to trip and fall in the darkness. 
He had always been a dutiful father who acted rather than lectured. His name, Jianshan, meant "builder of Hongshan". When Chichi first learned about his actual name, she laughed and said that it was too down-to-earth, like a hard and stubborn stone. The stone was the ballast that secured their life in the Hongshan Crater. The stone restrained its ability to skip across rivers and lakes, and sank itself into cities and civilization. The stone stayed behind, even after she left, and allowed itself to be covered in moss. 
And today the gate groaned again. Jianshan leaped up from his desk and went straight to the living room. His daughter kicked off her shoes, threw down her traveling satchel, and collapsed into the sofa. None of it felt normal. Jianshan counted the days in his mind. She stayed for three days during the new year holidays and had not been back for six months afterwards. Her return to Hongshan in an ordinary Monday afternoon was strange. Her credit card reported no expenses for nearly four days. How did she survive? And why did she look so tired and exhausted? Did she take the wrong bus? Hongshan Crater was known for its complex geography and people who seldom returned often messed up the rides and had to walk long detours to be home — But Jianshan kept all these questions to himself. 
"Hungry?" 
His darling girl nodded. 
He made some noodles and added two extra pieces of meat. The young lass was still growing. 
Qianyu came to the kitchen and served the table. She did not forget Chichi's rules despite romping through the world for fourteen months. They sat facing each other and had their meals. 
"What experiments have you been running, Dad?" 
"You probably won't know much about it." 
"Well, it'd be great if you cook as well as you do science. Your tests got all those generous HAS grants." 
"Your mom likes what I make." 
"Does that mean Mom had no taste? This is really salty." 
No matter the conversation, she would typically finish everything, even the soup. But this day was different. She set her chopsticks aside after two bites, and just sat on the chair as her eyes gazed outside. 
"Dad, I think I have trouble staying at a single place for long." 
He knew that Chen was clear that he could not and would not say anything, and probably did not know how to continue this topic. He usually just let the discussion slide. But her drooping tail and expressions looked particularly sad on this day. He suddenly realized that his prodigal daughter had matured somewhat, and was slowly learning her lessons. 
"Coals on your feet?" Guang Jianshan asked, "Your old man used to be a pretty fast runner. I can't afford to be slow, or your mama's blade would catch up to me." 
"What are you talking about?" 
"I used to hike the mountains carrying a hundred kilos of surveillance gear. You've seen them before. Big telescopes? It's always down to the training. The old Tianshi would fly around and lead the way while we ran along the foot of the mountains and tried to keep up..." 
"Ugh. Stop it already...! Hooo. I don't think I can find a place that fits me." 
She raised her head. The resemblance hit him and left him a little dazed. 
"Well, your ma... She actually left Hongshan three times. And that's just counting this place." 
"What? Why didn't you tell about this?!" 
"Because you probably won't understand." 
Jianshan saw the glimmer and spark return to his daughter's face. Chen was back, and quickly enough. 
"When did all this happen? Before I was born? Or when you moved back to Hongshan? Was that the last time she left? You told me she went to that Rho..." 
"Push me all you want. Your mama told me to keep it from you." 
"Ahhhhh! That silly old woman! Why?!" 
He looked at the girl who started eating her noodles once more. 
"So when are you moving out again?" </>

Every version of the Martial Codex includes records of Yanese spearmancy such as Spear of Empyrean Return and Pear Blossom Spear of Wuling. But one of the versions made a super exaggerated claim that ancient Tianshi could flick the sun and moon with their spears. They even furnished this section with great warriors of questionable authenticity flying all over the place (for details, refer to the Wrankwood movie industry during the Age of Terra, plenty of their stuff is based on false fantasies). The Martial Codex we have in the EFDB might be a dry and boring read, but it contains detailed records and identities of the practitioners and masters of various spearmancy schools. The Codex even has commentaries and suggestions written by the practitioners themselves. The Codex has detailed descriptions of everything from folk martial artists to Imperial Guards of Yan, Silverlance Pegasi of Kazimierz, wielders of Victorian piledriver spears, and even Kazdelian mercenaries. The author is truly admirable for being able to secure such a huge range of resources while giving off the vibe of being on equal standing of numerous legends! The commentaries were also written in a concise yet vivid style. It takes great conviction to achieve this. Hence, I truly believe that the Martial Codex in the EFDB is the original from the Age of Terra. The others that we can easily buy are just crude and exaggerated copies. A true shame, if you ask me.

It was late at night. You saw smoke billowing from the next door workshop. The ringing of hammer striking the anvil could be heard within a three block radius. It was deliberate. It was loud.
"What is she trying to prove?" you didn't want to care, but suddenly remembered the maniac next door mumbling about the near-completion of her work. Thus, you turned around and headed next door while putting on your jacket, all the while mumbling this to yourself, "Talos forbid if she actually forges it."
Glowing embers floated through the gap of the workshop door. You now regret putting on the jacket as the place was terrifyingly hot. The light of the fire also lured in the tramp who lived three blocks away. She wore something cooler, and started scoffing at you right from the get-go.
"Idiot. Look at you, all bundled up. When was the last time you lit your smithy's furnace?" The tramp always talked like this since she could crawl. She envenomed her weapons with her spit.
You ignored her and pushed open the door. The entire house was awash by the fiery glow of the forge. The maniac stood besides it, and unleashed a hysterical riot of a laughter when she saw you two enter her workshop.
"You're too late! I shall be the one giving life to this weapon!" The maniac was wholly drenched in sweat. You saw only fanatical zealotry on her face.
The tramp got closer to the forge and studied the roiling hot ferrium. Her tone turned somber as she delivered these words: "This is bad. She's going to forge it."
Envy surged from your guts. You felt like vomiting.
You hated each other's guts, but the three of you were once the best of friends. You forgot how the hate actually started, or you grew up together. Even all those evenings you spent drinking together escaped your memories. The only thing you recalled was that prophecy spreading throughout Seš'qa: "A legendary weapon shall be born this winter. And only three smiths could hope to achieve this feat." As luck (or misfortune) would have it, the three of you happen to be the best smiths of the city.
Since then, all three of you became obsessed with forging the legendary weapon before the other two. Every meeting became a scheme and an attempt to beat the other senseless and throw them out of the city.
Both you and the tramp had nothing to say at this moment. A skilled smith need only look at the fire to know the immense power it held. The maniac worked the bellows to raise the furnace temperature, but try as she might, the furnace refused to get any hotter. She sighed and wiped away the sweat from her face.
The tramp's face darkened as she gloated: "You are going to fail."
The maniac, however, did not even bat an eye at you. She simply laughed: "Far from it!" And with that, she slit open her throat. Hot blood gushed out like lava and flowed into the furnace.
You and the tramp stretched out your hands together but it was too late. The maniac fell into the furnace and a deafening explosion echoed throughout the town. Fire spluttered out of the furnace chamber and spread throughout the entire workshop. The flames roared with greater fury and threatened to end the night itself. Even the skies feared what was about to happen, and desperately unloaded a great snow to put out the fire.
As the temperature continued its rapid rise, you looked at the tramp for a word. But decades of tacit understanding tell you that nothing needed to be said.
You approached the fire, ignored the painful burns, and worked the bellows once more. The nascent weapon within the forge hummed and complained. It was not hot enough. The temperature is too low. It demanded a flame with enough heat to sear a hole through the skies. The tramp sneered as you saw the blaze dancing in her eyes, a conflagration of fury, pain, regret, and ambition. Fire burst from her eyes and swallowed her whole. You had no time to grieve for the snowstorm of the night was relentless. It would do anything to put out their fires.
You were the idiot of the group who never mastered the Arts. The only recourse you had was better and more precise controls over the bellows for firing up the heat. Years of experience made you a master of keeping the fire going. The bellows swelled and emptied as the fire danced and howled. The flaming tongues licked your skin and it slowly gave way like molten wax. But the mere thought of the weapon maturing into its form gave you incredible elation and made you beam with satisfaction.
Did it hurt? It was far less painful than the last fight you had when the maniac tore a piece off your face with her teeth.
Before the flames completely devoured you, you finally remembered how they laughed with merriment back in the tavern.
The flames might not endure against the night-long blizzard, and there would be no trace of the three of you after the workshop fire. Nevertheless, you knew that a fireplace would remain, and within it they would find a sword capable of cleaving anything in the world apart.

4. Aburrey Quarry: Signal lost. Suspected damage to the camera affixed to the Landbreaker; said entity has been attacked and eliminated by the enemy. 
5. Bridge Approach Camp: Several Landbreakers had left or joined the retreating column. Only a few fuzzy videos have been captured. Final position has been abandoned. 
6. United Parking Lot, Originium Power Plant: Focus all cameras on Camille Arno and the Endministrator of Endfield Industries. Monitor the activities of these two individuals. 
...... 
This report proves that an unknown party has deployed a well-hidden monitoring system throughout the region of Valley IV. 

Nobody could have imagined that the Endministrator returned from this trip with several thousand hours worth of video recordings. The discovery, found in an abandoned underground facility, left every analyst in shock. It proves that an organization has been acting from the shadows of Valley IV, silently observing every action of everyone, and pulling secret strings to exert control over the region. 
When the analysts realized that the cameras were implanted within the Landbreakers to avoid detection (Camille mentioned how the perpetrator abandoned them without second thought), they knew why Seš'qa chose to assign an Agaš'mekanaz to the task. Fortunately, after Camille Arno arrived at Valley IV, all the cameras were assigned to monitor his movement and activities. The period of monitoring happens to overlap with Endfield activities in the region. We can safely assume that no pieces of critical intel have been leaked. The lack of leakage is also why none of our operators noticed the unwarranted third-party monitoring. 
After receiving the video feed, operators of the tech division traced the origins to an earlier batch of records (already destroyed) and realized that the organization had begun tracking Camille several decades ago. Though the Keeper himself responded to this finding mildly and appeared to have expected this, the techies sympathized with his plight and promised to give his equipment a suite of upgrades designed to counter covert monitoring measures. When the analysts briefed Camille about their findings, he just leaned against the wall and looked at the screen quietly for quite a while before he raised his eyes and asked: "Say if you were on the other side of the monitoring cameras, staring at a familiar person ... what is most likely to come to mind?" 
The analysts gave all sorts of answers. Camille did not respond to any of them but continued his extended silence. Finally, he left a written note in the debriefing report. 
"So much alike, yet so divergent in essence. Why?" 
He wants the answer to the question. He needs it.

Kjersch was snowing again. There were no winds that day. The snowflakes fell right into the tomb. 
"Too cold," thought the messenger who stood next to the resting place. He trembled and held tightly onto the cup of warm tea in his hands. "But why is it that gentleman ... seems unfazed by the cold?" He lifted his gaze and saw the peaks wrapped in a mist that a flicker of golden ray made through. With squinted eyes he studied it. It was the Arts Unit brought by the Collector, and it looked like very antique as well. 
Seven years had passed since he accepted this commission. He lost count of how many times he scaled the mountain or how many packages he had delivered. 
Every package was important. The Collector kept telling him that. Every one of them was the final heirloom for the surviving family of the deceased. A successful delivery must be ensured. 
The deceased. A distant and cold word. That was what the Collector called the people buried in the snowy mount. But when he entered the cemetery, the Collector would become focused beyond measure. He would tell stories about them as though he was the closest acquaintance that the poor souls ever had. 
—Beneath a pile of stones wrapped with three colorful ribbons rested a young, energetic Perro. A lad who passed away before he reached the North Pole. 
—Under a mound of black rocks at the northeast laid a most powerful Forte warrior, one who ran like the wind despite burdened by the heaviest supplies. 
—As for this heap of gray pebbles, whose ribbons had long lost their colors, it was the cold bed for... 
Who was it? The messenger's memory failed him. Perhaps only the Collector knew the stories of everyone. 
"That old gent really seems to know everyone," the messenger mused. It was really odd. Some tombs were not made ten years ago. As per the traditions of Kjersch, older tombs could be identified with their higher mounds. The messenger was willing to bet that the biggest mound was at least half a century old. 
Perhaps the Collector experienced more than just the Polar Expedition. Perhaps he had more stories than he could even imagine. 
"The cold bites. Apologies for keeping you here for this long," the Collector suddenly walked over and interrupted the messenger's train of ideas. 
The messenger quickly shook his head and gave the cup of tea, brewed in advance, to the gent. "Something to ward off the cold, sir. And what would be the package for today? I have to expedite this delivery as we have an incoming snowstorm this afternoon. Things might get difficult if they stop the cable cars." 
"Just this," the Collector takes up the Arts Unit that flickered with a faint glow. "This is the last, as all the other heirlooms have been delivered. This would be your last hike for the deliveries. Take these Talosian credit notes. Free yourself from the abuses of nature and start a business at the foot of this mountain." 
The messenger took the thick stack of notes. This seven-year commission finally ended. Yet after all those years of deliveries, he still did not know the Collector's name, where he was from, nor where he intended to go. 
Perhaps the Collector read the messenger's mind as the latter hesitated for a while. "Do you have question for me?" 
"Saw right through me, sir. I'm just curious. All these years you told me so many stories from the past, but all of them were about other people. What about you? You took part in many battles. Don't you have stories about yourself?" 
The Collector became quiet. 
The snowstorm was at the very threshold of the mountain. The winds grew stronger and lifted his silvery hair. It came with such a force that the messenger could barely see the Collector's face. 
Quite a moment passed before the messenger heard the Collector's answer. 
"I regard the expedition ... as a probation of self-deceit." 
The snow continued. A slow shower of crystalline flakes that fell on heads of the living, and the tombs of the deceased.

<@profile.key>DOCUMENT: A private letter 
Eyrwin: 
Maybe I should call you Snowshine now. In any case, please forgive me for not saying goodbye when I left the team... That was never my intention. But my captain and my attending surgeon, Margarit, told me to leave the north immediately. They said it would prevent my hallucinations from getting worse. 
Kjersch is a beautiful city. We don't see any auroras here but there are equally majestic mountains in snow. The ridges are untouched by the Blight or the Aggeloi, and are linked by criss-crossing cable tramways that the city is so famous for — I took quite a few rides in them, and the experience of gazing into the vast snowfields without worry is unforgettable... 
You must have been surprised by my decision. Someone who had sworn to stay in the north and the SAR team for eternity ... was suddenly beaten by a most mundane and ordinary blizzard. What I want to say is that sometimes people are not as strong as they like to think. Perhaps I'm actually more fragile than I think I was. 
I never feared blizzards, the Blight, or any other disasters that could suddenly swoop in and take our lives. But when I saw Nelson lose a leg after getting sucked into the Blight while trying to save that unlucky prospector ... and after learning that Lisa lost her sight from overexerting her Originium Arts to give everyone an early warning... I started doubting myself. I began to think if I had fallen short ... and my suspicions soon spread to other members of the team... 
I have the captain to thank. I was about to use the Arts Unit when he stopped me and ordered Medical Officer Margarit to give Ryder the timely treatment he needed... He saved me from doing something I would've regretted for the rest of my life. Eyrwin, of all the young people on the team, I have the highest expectations for you. In fact, I believe you are the perfect candidate to succeed as deputy captain. You value friendship and care for others deeply, often to the point of neglecting your own safety. So take this as advice from someone who's been through it: never forget to look after yourself, especially when you're out there saving others. 
You are important and irreplaceable to the SAR team and everyone who cares for you. 
I look forward to your reply. Feel free to let me play the host in your visit to Kjersch. And try to bring the captain along. I'll take you all to the best fondue in town. It tastes exactly like what you described to me. 

Madeleine Crick 

DOCUMENT: A private letter 
Madeleine: 
Thank you for writing to me! 
Even now, I still remember your patience when you first taught me how to build an igloo shelter in the snowfields; your stern expression when you reminded me that every SAR teammate must maintain constant vigilance; and your tenderness when you helped me fix my drone at 4 AM, telling me to be more careful next time. These are precious memories I'll carry with me for the rest of my life... 
So, I have never doubted your passion for SAR operations. Even though you have left the north, I believe you're still helping everyone at your new place in your own special ways. 
Ryder and the captain refused to tell me what exactly happened on the mountain, but I could sort of guess from the operational logs... I don't think they, or anyone for that matter, would blame you for this. So I hope you can focus on getting better, and don't forget to explore the place when have time. Once I swing by Kjersch (captain seems pretty busy and I couldn't get hold of him) I'll definitely pay you a visit. And is that fondue place really as good as you say? I really wanna try it out! 
P.S. The pack that came with this letter is your favorite sundried berries. Eat them before they expire! 

Eyrwin </>

<@profile.key>No Op Z7 teammates, except for Estella, have positive memories regarding the anniversary for the Founding of Operations Team Z7. However, everyone agrees that it was an unforgettable occasion. 
At first, Akekuri found that the team had no field assignments on the day of the anniversary and suggested celebrating the occasion. Everyone responded positively and a discussion on the means of celebration began. However, since the team was encamped in the wildlands far from the Civilization Band, every suggestion involved some form of outdoor activity. Estella, unwilling to engage in any physical exertion, naturally voted against every single proposal. In the end, "riverside picnic" was the only option that received a unanimous vote. It was not the favorite option for everyone, but at least nobody voted against it. 
On the day of the anniversary, everyone was eagerly gathering herbs and hunting game. Estella, however, returned with an armful of colorful mushrooms. Her teammates firmly rejected her suggestion to toss those wild fungi into the cooking pot. In the end, the team conceded. Under Captain Akekuri's watchful eyes, several unassuming mushrooms were allowed to be part of the stew. 
As the sun set, the team built a campfire by the river to enjoy what they had gathered throughout the day. Fortunately, the "unassuming" mushrooms turned out to be only mildly toxic. Unfortunately, they were incredibly spicy. The team emptied their water canteens to douse the heat but to no avail. Desperate, they rushed to the riverbank to wash the spicy taste away with river water. That's when they heard a low rumble coming from upstream — the dam had begun a reservoir drawdown! 
"Curses! I forgot about the UWST reservoir drawdown notice! That's why there's no field operations today!" 
No one remembered exactly how they ended up swept away by the floodwaters. When they finally came to, they found Estella skillfully surfing the rushing water on the team's cooking pot. The sun had already set when the four Op Z7 teammates pulled each other to shore. They had no choice but head downstream to look for Estella. Finally, the team found Estella sound asleep at a nomad campfire in wee hours of the morning. The nomads treated Akekuri and her team to a proper wildlands feast. 
The nomads were extremely accommodating and the team decided to rest there for the night. Just as Akekuri was about to fall asleep beneath the starry ceiling, she suddenly remembered a Z7 field assignment in a few hours' time. Estella could not be awakened, so the four Z7 teammates took turns carrying her. They successfully reached the Endfield camp at daybreak. 
According to Estella's memories, she was completely unconscious as she probably ate the other fungi she picked. She treated the flood waters as a packed and riotous moshpit, and fantasized herself as a rockstar performing a stage dive and surfing the crowd while she growled and screamed her songs. Nobody knew what Estella sang. Akekuri only remembered how she carried Estella and trudged back to camp. The young girl on her back did mumble a few things while she slept — things about home.</>

As the great guns thundered into the skies, night finally returned to Fort Forgefane. The steam stopped hissing as the last Aggelos was crushed into gravel. Victory trumpeted throughout the icefields, the clarion call of triumph echoed amongst collapsed bastions before it reached a stone crypt used as a provisional morgue to house the fallen warriors.
To the smiths of Fort Forgefane, the clarion call felt more like a final farewell to the soldier. A forgesmith pulled a cart of salvaged equipment and paused before a young Oathkeeper, long bereft of breath.
Why did the smith stop? Was it his fear of death? He did not think so. He dreamed about falling like a true Oathkeeper soldier from the day he submitted his enlisting papers to the Order of Steel Oath. And since his first arrival at the gates of Fort Forgefane, he was determined to be a nail, permanently hammered into his post. There were only two things that could stop him from swinging his hammer: the future he dreamed had been achieved, or it became necessary for someone else to take his post.
The smith stooped over and took the long sword from the hands of the young soldier.
He could not remove his gaze from the soldier's face. Was he paying his final respects to a former comrade? No. He had said his farewells to all sorts of people in the south before he marched for the north. He saw his loved ones secretly weeping for his sake, witnessed the reluctance in their eyes, and even attended a close friend's funeral on the night before he reported to the training camp.
But what he felt at this very moment was new. A mysterious surge of emotions gripped him to the ground, even though he tried, again and again, to get himself to leave.
Heavy footsteps echoed in the crypt. The smith raised his head and held his breath.
"Lord Castellan Gerald! Apologies, I'm just ... salvaging the equipment."
The armored giant stretched out his hand and took the blade from the smith. The edge was curled and a fine crack ran along its length.
"Do you know him?"
"No... We're not familiar. But I did share some drink with him in the welcoming feast held for us several days ago..."
"What do you intend to do with this blade?"
The smith took the blade and shook off the snow from the hilt. He carefully studied the wounds suffered by the weapon and gave his verdict: "It will be my honor to return this blade to the furnace and have it recast, and the joy will be equal to seeing you throw this Aggeloid host back to whence they came. He is a hero ... that no one will remember."
"He is also a common man, just as common as this blade."
"My Lord Castellan... what would you have me do to this blade?"
"Even the perfect blade will one day shatter," Gerald patted the smith on the shoulder. "It shall be returned to the forge, pass through the ranks of Oathkeepers, and fulfill his unfinished duty."

Can you believe it, Lonna? I'm not on Talos-II when delivering this letter. 
You probably guessed it too. That's right! I was part of the special delegation from the Talos-II General Chamber of Commerce, and we were attending a closed-door meeting with Endfield aboard their ship, Dijiang. 
It was my first time boarding a vessel capable of traversing the sea of stars. And what a sea it is! It's far deeper and quieter than the oceans we have, with faint stars glittering in the distance. From space, Talos-II looks just like baby Baily fast asleep in his crib. 
Oh, my cute little Baily. Give our sweet baby a kiss on the head for me. 
I thought all my curiosities could be satisfied by the stars and the view of Talos-II from space, but on day four, Endfield arranged something special for us as part of the reception. We visited their zero gravity experience chamber. It looked like a simple, empty room. When we were ready, the lights grew dim and the sky window slowly opened, allowing the light from Talos the gas giant to pour in. The huge planet seized all of our attention. 
And then, gravity itself disappeared. 
Even for our negotiators and corporate officers. All of them lost their solemn gravity and instincts took over. My ears were filled with gasps of astonishment and wonder. I even heard a soft chuckle, and I swear it came from the Endfield operator who served as our guide. Looking at big-timer suits acting like playful or scared children must have offered a pure sense of joy. If this wasn't a closed-door and confidential meeting, the walls of this zero-g chamber would be plastered with photos of its "victims". 
As for me... I don't know how to say this to you, Lonna. When I floated in the sky, abandoned by every ounce of my weight and by the land itself, a refreshing sense of freedom coursed through my body as I faced the celestial object before me. I... 
I felt a sense of duty. 
A sense of the most impossible duty. 
I suddenly felt compelled to bring this experience to every resident of the Civilization Band. 
We are the children born into the cradle of Talosian gravity. But the birth of Dijiang would be the first time in our history when we finally have the chance to live differently. 
I remember father telling me that the most priceless thing is not a luxurious mansion or merchandise. That honor goes to the way of life. 
Can anything be more special than transcending the grips of gravity and living amongst the stars? 
We'll get an artificial geostationary orbit experience cabins in the future. We start from the basics, then work our way towards commercial complexes and space arenas. Every sport will get new rules, new tournaments, and new superstars competing in the zero-g environment. When knights wearing jet packs rocket through arenas, when race cars make perfect turns across toroid tracks, when the football flies into the goal under the influence of mechanics and gravity... When all these happen, our achievements will far outstrip any sum of money we imagined, Lonna. 
Of course, none of this would be possible without your support, dear. Do remember to take a look at the attached design drawings. Even if we didn't get the chance to pull it off, at least we can leave our ideas for posterity. If I secured your approval with proposal, then let us try to build this together and submit this to the concept design event. The company and the TGCC will remember it for us. 
I'll be back soon, but I really hope to hear back from you when I reach home, Lonna. 
Love you. 

NOTE: A design draft is attached to this letter. A table listing the manufacturing specifications is provided at the lower right corner of the draft. A temporary name has also been proposed: 
"Junction Point"

"She may come off as cold and heartless, but that is what's needed in the YSTF." A bystander's evaluation of Li Zhiyan is usually very simple. 
All of Li's actions and choices can be boiled down to this statement: Finishing the mission. The troopers of the Yinglung Special Task Force (YSTF) always fight in extreme environments. Cold rationality and sheer determination help guarantee the success of a mission. If "safe exit" is not listed as part of the mission objective, every Yinglung knew what it meant. 
The YSTF has a secret chamber kept under tight security. They do not use it for storing intel files or documents, but for the "belongings" of every Yinglung. When you become an Yinglung, you are given a box and you are free to put anything you want in it. In the event that you fall during a mission, that thing in the box will function as the only proof of your existence. 
But Li Zhiyan's box remained empty. 
She told the chamber custodian that she had nothing. Everything she once had was buried within the dark, cold, and toxic Miasma of the North Wuling Exclusion Zone. 
The custodian had to tell her that this was a YSTF rule. It made Li think. What item best represents herself? If the title of YSTF Captain were taken from her, is there anything that she could put in the box? She pondered about the meaning of "self". 
She was only temporarily hampered by the question. Soon enough, she found an old artist on the market to write her name down with a calligraphy brush. This name was the thing that entered the box. 
The question did not feel important to her. It was the next mission that always mattered most. 
...... 
Li barely visited the secret chamber until recently. In her multiple visits, her once threadbare box began to fill. A pen. A button. A dagger also joined the pile... Every item appeared mundane and meaningless, as though she just grabbed something from the desk. A few seemed like gifts from her neighbors or keepsakes that someone wanted her to pass on... Yet Li treated them all like treasure and carefully placed them in her box. 
When a curious Endministrator asked about this, Li no longer responded with stern silence as she'd often done in the past. Instead, she gave a solemn answer. 
"I looked back and realized that I have missed so many things that I should have treasured."

Camille always thought his emotions were well-hidden away. When compared to other operators who exercised zero restraints, he did a fine job. Unfortunately, unintended movements and barely noticeable body language still betrayed him. 
When frustrated, Camille would lower his gaze and study a crack, if any, on the ground, or subconsciously rub his shoulder blade. When he wishes to avoid contact, he would shift his center of balance to his right leg to expedite immediate flight. When hesitating or discomforted, his fingers would subconsciously rub the old, ancient key hanging from his waist. 
Many Endfield operators have an item or keepsake they focus on. For example, Yvonne treats Frost-e-Bytee as a close friend, Rossi has her dagger, and Da Pan is always carrying that ferrium wok on his back. But Camille is different. If anyone were to ask him about his key, he would immediately retract his hand as though the thing had become a burning brand. He would keep his lips tightly closed and refuse to respond to the inquiry. 
Skilled machinists would identify that the key was a handcrafted from something that resembled a music box cylinder, though Camille knows nothing about artisanry. The man has no property to his name, and no one knows what the key could actually open. 
Eventually, everyone became wiser and learned not to ask about the item. 
In the end, Camille confessed to the origins of the key during a casual conversation. It was a present personally crafted by his younger brother (the very same who broke all ties with him). It was part of their home at Seš'qa, which Camille later sold after an accident and no longer returned to. The key was merely ornamental and his habit of touching the key was rooted in longing ... and perhaps a dash of inexplicable ennui. After saying these words, Camille placed the key in one of his pockets. 
What he remembered was the searing pain as if a chunk of flesh were being torn from his body, and a dark and exhausting past that went on and on. The gift was offered when sincerity remained. The Keeper faced a dilemma, and he no longer wanted to be reminded. 
A few days later, Camille received a Baker toast and visited the Endministrator's office. He was received by a smiling Endministrator who dropped a new key into his hands. 
"Such keys and locks are pretty rare, so making them took quite a while," the person said, "I just want you to know that Dijiang always has a door that you can open." 
It caught Camille by surprise. He tightly wrapped his fingers around the key and turned his face aside. He tried to form words, but they came out like noises made by a wheezing fowl whose neck was caught in an iron grip. In the end, he only managed to blurt out a barely audible phrase: "Thank you." 
Not everybody is familiar with Camille's body language, but everyone knows that the jingling of the new key against the old is joyous, like how he felt at that very moment.

<@profile.key>"I really like Tianshi Zhuang, but I don't seem to know her well." Every operator who worked with her feels this way. 
Tianshi Zhuang's past is easy to trace. Any visitor to Wuling City can get the basics from a local tour guide or receptionist. For those who wish to know more, simply dig deeper into the archives of the Tianshi Bureau Academy to peruse her publications, though reading them all takes some dedication. And those who manage to do all that would have a clear picture of the Tianshi — A scientist deeply immersed in her work, a Viceroy who has dutifully served Wuling for a decade. 
If you wish to set aside Tianshi Zhuang's titles and know her personally, seek out an opportunity to be her coworker. Most people describe their first impression of her as the soothing gusts of Wuling City in March: gentle, comforting, and refreshing. As a coworker, Zhuang could unravel even the most recalcitrant of problems. She would be the cool midsummer breeze that takes away frustration and restores balance. The comfortable peace would last until your experiment hits a bottleneck. And then you'd sense a storm quietly brewing beneath her composed exterior. 
Her speech would change. It becomes quick and relentless, like a sudden downpour of which few can keep pace. Her stride would quicken. Every step a violent gust, sending reports flapping and fluttering off the tabletops. And finally, her problem-solving would transform. Like a blitz, she strikes directly at the source of the issue to completely shatter it, a guiding flash of light in the face of doom and gloom. 
Soon enough, the problem is no more. The storm subsides. 
You might think you know Tianshi Zhuang after several tumultuous rounds of collaboration. But as you catch your breath, you would realize that you only saw her scholarly side of Her Viceroyalty more clearly. And then it hits you: she never talks about herself. Not to you, not to anyone. 
You had stepped into the eye of the storm — and found nothing but stillness.

I met them in the wilderness.
They were not friendly at first. One of their Aldertones inspected my wounds and permitted me to stay until I became well enough to move on my own. The others, however, refused to converse with me. Perhaps this was the price that I had to pay for wearing a uniform of TGCC origin.
Their way of life left quite ... an impression on me. These people developed a unique culture centered around the idea of "simplicity". No. "Restraint" would be a better word. They might not have the best technology, but they made the most out of every material. These people crafted tools with a unique minimalist aesthetic — a style of beauty molded by the harsh and unforgiving wildlands of this untamed world.
I told them I was a crafter and it gave me a chance to take part in their work. Observing their craftsmanship up close gave me a rather shocking revelation — their weapons were fashioned using far less materials and simpler processes, but overall performance was only marginally less than our TGCC counterparts. This discovery made me realize that our designs actually have plenty of room for improvement.
I left the Circuit after spending three whole years with them, and they gave me honors befitting their own Aldertones. Deep down, I learned far more from the people of the Circuit than what I taught them in return.

<@profile.key>Wulfgard knew better than anyone, that leaving the Pack for good meant this journey had no return date. By his own standards, that meant packing everything that might prove useful. 
Yet, standing before Il Cacciatore and sweeping his gaze over the massive rig that had been his and his sister's home for nearly a decade... he realized, abruptly, that there was nothing left worth taking. 
He went over his plans once more in his mind: make sure Rossi knew exactly who in the clan could be trusted, confirm the two ways people could reach him, ask Tommaso to keep a close watch over Rossi, settle the last bit of custom work fees at Uncle Rust's, feed Giovanni's semi-wild fowlbeasts one last time, entrust them to little Vincenzo next door... No, he hasn't forgotten a thing. 
Satisfied, he turned for one final check. Just to be absolutely sure he hadn’t left Rossi's handmade Originium lamp glowing on the bedside table. 
But as soon as he stepped into his sleeping compartment, his eyes caught sight of something in an unremarkable corner of the cabinet: his worn guns — the very first weapons he'd ever owned. 
Though secondhand and now running low on compatible ammo, those guns were priceless treasures back then. They kept him and his sister alive, earned him his first mercenary contract, and helped him take down his first target. When one of the Originium activators failed, he was forced to master one-handed reloads and gun maintenance. After three years of supporting his family with mercenary pay, he finally replaced the worn Originium activator and even crafted a set of custom-etched ammo. 
These guns were passed down from the clan's elders. Like many inherited dreams, they met their end during a high-stakes escort mission, overheating after prolonged firing. 
Soon after, Uncle Rust — a bounty hunter who had returned to the Pack and opened a weapon refurbishment shop called "Howlfire Gunsmiths." There, Wulfgard was introduced to custom weapon modifications for the first time. 
Then he learned to make weapons truly his own, even if they only suited him. 
Still, he never got rid of those guns that got him started. They remained tucked away in a quiet corner. 
Why keep them? As a reminder? A keepsake? Or a memento of painful memories? 
He wasn't sure — maybe all, maybe none. 
After confirming the Originium lamp was off, he headed for the door, ready to embark on a journey that might finally give him an answer.</>

-4705231213366901567:
Not everyone's heart was mine to touch, but I could read my own like a book.
In this very instant, my heart is filled with nothing but fear. Our science station, the "observatory" we constructed to defeat the boundless Very Large Rift, has been engulfed by the Blight and despair did likewise to my mind. Will the Xiranite succeed? Is the entirety of our efforts completely meaningless? The Æther made us realize how insignificant we are. It will devour Wuling and everything in existence. How are we supposed to oppose this astronomical phenomenon?
......
A canal must be constructed. Although rescue work of victims from the disaster site is top priority right now, this canal is of utmost necessity. It will prevent the aquifers from contamination by the Blight Tide seeping into the soil. But this is ultimately futile. It only delays the inevitable death of everything upon this land.
......
My hands are covered in blisters. Though I'm just a worker at the production floor with zero knowledge on construction, I have been assigned to a building crew... We must fight off the disaster until reinforcements arrive from our HQ.
......
I got a cut in my hand. I unearthed a broken dagger from the canal construction site. How long has it been buried here? A century? By Talos, take a good look at your bleeding hand! To hell with glory and sacrifice! Why am I still alive? Why do I want to be alive? Why should I be alive at all? WHY?
......
Blighted hell. I'll off myself tomorrow.
......
I chose the night. At the construction site. Good place. Perfect weather, with pouring rain that soaks everything in the friggin' mud. Losers like us deserve to die and get buried in the mud.
The rain-swollen torrents tore through the last unfinished section of the canal. I spotted a metallic sheen in the freshly exposed mud. I don't know why I walked over to the glint and scooped out the mud with my bare hands. I unearthed the thing buried beneath — a rusty valve.
That was it.
Ours was an ad-hoc rush job with neither infrastructure map data nor verification. And as chance would have it, we completed the canal that our predecessors failed to finish.
My view of the thoroughly rusted valve transformed at once. It was my father's will, my mother's portrait, the paper flowers offered to my grandparents' grave...
...and me... I saw my reflection in the muddy water.
That was it.
Someone always wanted to survive. And someone always survived.
The heavens and earth are not without boundaries. Fear itself could disintegrate completely.
With that, I stopped thinking about death.
I but extend the facet of survival and persistence, the never-ending cycle that has endured for since time immemorial.

I think I need to retire.
There is nothing to be had on this world.
Did we make any great findings after 10 years and nearly 30 major excavation attempts? No. We found only engines of war that the Ursine were forced to abandon in the Great Rift Valley and the ruins of automated pastures given up to the hosts of Aggeloi and the never-ending Blight.
These discoveries were little more than rotting crates of our mundane past.
The true history of Talos-II would be the ruins left behind by our ancestors — And I unearthed 3 of these sites. All were empty. We found no bodies, no sources of power, and no machineries. There was nothing. Nothing but shards of metal. They did give off a light that I could peer into. I saw fuzzy images of our ancestors who lived eons ago. I saw them smile. The smiles looked genuine. Our ancestors looked happy.
None of our discoveries revealed what happened before us. In fact, our very own past remains shrouded. Talos-II continues to hide behind the obscuring veil. A Songseeker of the Hannabit Circuit told me their very first Aldertone caught a glimpse of the world's shadowy past in the frozen icefields. This tiny glimpse scarred her with a monumental terror greater than Talos itself.
I told this to an Oathkeeper friend of mine. She replied with her own tale. Whenever she stood atop the Order fortress walls and gazed into the thick dark clouds that smothered the northern skies, she could feel the planet's shadow lurking behind it. This shadow would briefly retreat whenever she stepped onto the battlefield.
"Be strong, and do not think too much about it."
Those were her words when she gave me her handcannons.   Fine. I'm putting off the retirement. I'm heading out there again.

<@profile.key>Results of Operator Chen Qianyu's background checks are not complicated. The operator is as consistent, simple, and straightforward as she appears. 
Operator Chen Qianyu grew up in the Hongshan Crater and studied swordmancy at Tanjian Hall. Prior to joining Endfield, she has interned at various organizations and served different individual employers. Hence, in spite of her young age, Operator Chen has years of solo combat experiences. After a period of adjustment, she has now grown used to team-based combat. 
Unlike many youths who lost their parents in pioneering operations in the unforgiving and disaster-ridden lands of Talos-II, Chen Qianyu grew up in a wholesome and happy family. Her relatively simple childhood also gave her unshakable optimism. She is often praised for her excellent teamwork and sunny personality in multiple instances of team-based operations. Many key collaborators, including Chief Engineer Andre, have high hopes for Operator Chen and believe that she is a poster child for a certain facet of Endfield: Young, positive, friendly, and eager to intercede and solve any problem that needs to be solved. 

[ADDITIONAL NOTES] 
During early contact, we realized that Operator Chen Qianyu has, without question or doubt, earned stellar performance reviews at multiple employers. However, many are still curious why she never stayed at any particular employer for extended periods of time. To date, Operator Chen has spent the longest period of time working for Endfield. We asked her this question during a regular interview and her answers are provided below: 
"Cheers and Drinks at La Fantoma? Wait, did I actually work there for three months?! Yeah, that's easy to explain. I had my fill of the milk tea so I left." 
"Oh... Temporary security personnel. Yeah, I wasn't old enough to get an actual job but I really needed the money for my next stop. My only choice was to work in EXPOs and conferences. But yeah, those were the months when I met plenty of big shots in Talos-II..." 
"Hold on! My graduation year performance at Tanjian Hall is actually — EXCELLENT?! Wait! You're not reading it wrong, right? I ... well, it's normal for me to be clueless about this! Heheh! "I spent more than a year in Yinglung Special Task Force... Yeah, I did that, but can we not talk about this? Well, there's nothing to hide. I just don't find the place a good match for me. Wha? Did you just say there are people who don't get along with me?! Okay, that's ridiculous! Know anything about Duccio the Half-Face? That notorious gang leader at the Asphalt Roundabout? I actually had a pretty nice convo with him, you know!"</>

<@profile.key>Before, reflecting on the past used to come naturally for Shiba Momiji. Back in school, she had a knack for breaking down a year's worth of progress with neat charts and detailed annotations — earning top grades with ease. 
But now, things are different. It's been a full year since Operations Team Z7 was formed. And instead of stats and milestones, what fills her heart now ... are feelings. 
She constantly worries about Catcher. As the team's shield and support, he looks after everyone like family. Is he overextending himself...? 
She pays attention to Estella's condition. Some may see her as unmotivated or laid-back, but Akekuri knows better. Estella is healing her own fragile body while quietly helping Op Z7 heal the world. That takes a rare kind of strength. 
She watches over Fluorite's moods, not just her frequent outbursts or headstrong ways. Akekuri often asks herself: Am I being a strong enough cushion? One that lets her feel understood and safe? 
She worries about Antal too. Often labeled an "odd one," Antal is, in truth, passionate and reliable — his way of connecting simply different. She sees how hard he's been working to keep pace with the team. 
It's because of them that Z7 stands as it does today. 
She's deeply grateful — for their trust, for their belief in her leadership, and for proving that this team, once seen as inexperienced, could stand on its own. 
But most of all, she wonders about herself: Has she met the expectations she set — using what little they had to help as many as possible ... and to find her own light in the process? 
Sometimes she wonders: if the ideals of Endfield are ever fulfilled, and peace finally comes — maybe, just maybe, her parents might reconcile. And perhaps she could go home, just like when she was little ... and share one peaceful family meal together again. 
She is giving her all to make that future possible. 

Annual Performance Report
SUBMITTED BY: Akekuri, Captain, Operations Team Z7 

Dear Supervisor Perlica, 
This report outlines the major operations and achievements of Operations Team Z7 over the past year. 
We completed 40 missions with a 95% success rate and zero casualties. These included 16 cross-region supply runs, 9 joint wildlands recon operations, 7 high-risk engineering escorts, and 8 emergency rescues. 
We've steadily grown from a provisional support force into a reliable, fully operational unit. 
P.S. While our combat rating remains average in this year's assessment, we ranked among the top in support, command, and management. 
......
Regarding the rumored awakening of the "Endministrator," though I have yet to witness it myself, I can feel the excitement in  stories shared by our seniors. If possible, I'd like to respectfully request that Operations Team Z7 be involved in missions under the Endministrator's command. It would be a privilege to personally deliver our tactical reports — and even more meaningful to work alongside the Endministrator to bring Endfield's vision to life. Together, we can restore peace to Talos-II...</>

[RECEIVING RECORD] 
RECIPIENT: Li Zhiyan 
SENDER: Ling Yue 
SENDER'S ADDRESS: Wuling City 
STATUS: Signed and received 
INSPECTION: Inspection passed 
VOICE MESSAGE: 
Zhiyan! It's me! Auntie Liu! I heard you're getting some R and R at Endfield. You should have told me, Ah Girl. The entire neighborhood got super worried! So I asked the young lady at Serenity Garden to help deliver some of your favorite things! Just a few boxes of osmanthus cakes and sweet kohl pudding. I brewed it just a few days ago for baby's birthday, so it won't keep forever. Finish it first, okay? 
Auntie Shen also cares a lot about you. She stuffed the package with a few sets of clothing that she sewed. She heard you're now staying on a spaceship and so she kept complaining how cold you are in space. So yes, that's where the clothes are from in case you're wondering. 
Ah Girl, I don't know when you'd be back. You've always been stubborn. Always sitting at one spot and doing nothing. You hardly played with other girls your age. Instead, you kept trying to help the aunties in the neighborhood. It's not right! You are a darling girl but we're getting old and won't be around forever. Listen to your Auntie and make some friends at Endfield. I saw their Endmin and the young lady called Perlica, and they look very nice to me! And if you don't know how to make small talk, just take the rice cakes and sweet kohl pudding to the Endfielders, and let them try out your Auntie's cooking! Do this a few times and you'll have new friends! 
Auntie watched you grow up. You never liked to talk, but Auntie knows you got an eye for details. I made a note every time you helped us. Remember when you returned with a photo of Auntie Shen's little girl? Auntie Shen couldn't stop crying that day. Poor girl left when she was around your age, so Auntie Shen treated you like her own. And ... it's the same for all of us. You are a child of Wuling. The city is always your home, no matter where you go. 
Aiyah, the talk is getting too sad. Auntie isn't very good with words, so maybe I should stop here. Just focus on getting better and try to come home early. Once you come back to Wuling, Auntie will make a huge feast for you! Don't forget about Auntie's advice! Bring your new friends too! 
...... 
Wait. Aiyo, Auntie Shen actually has something to say but she started crying again. I'll just let Ling Yue deliver the package and let Auntie Shen record a voice message later. Hope we're not bugging you. Hey! Don't rush me! I'm not taking forever, okay! Wait. Low battery? How —

Uncle Pan can transform and he's got all sorts of clothes like a big white shef apron or crew overalls. Sometimes he also wears a yellow plastic hat. Uncle Pan also has a hot pot shop and tolds us that we can have meals at his place if we miss home and if we got tired of hot pot he will make other delishus stuff like mantow buns, flashy fryd kidnees, or sweet sour fins. The best food made by Uncle Pan is the veeneger bokk choy and refryd meat and he wants to make them the chefs speshow. 
But sometimes Uncle Pan plays pranks on us. He puts spisy saos in my lunch box but tells me its magic jam so i share the magic jam with my frenz and everyone got sosejj lips. 
Uncle Pan takes care of the kids and he also helps other people. He can fix power meeters, do plumming and pipes, chop the bamboos. Cos Uncle Pan is so helpful to everyone, everyone also wants to help Uncle Pan. But Uncle Pan is reely powerfol and theres nothing we can help him with, so we gave him delishus fruits and sweets... and the landlord lowerd his hot pot shop rent. Peepo say that Uncle Pan is homeless cos his home eksploddeded so he has to spend money to liv in a frenz home. 

One day i ask Uncle Pan why he made no money after working for many years. He told me he spent all the money on food but later i lerned that he spent all the money on the kids... 
— Chen Qianyu 

His passion and friendliness are infectious. People often start spilling their beans and sharing their stories within minutes after meeting him. But the reverse does not apply. Operator Da Pan rarely talks about his own story. Nevertheless, many still regard him as the "friendly HAS tianshi who really knows how to cook". A painful past may be a burden to bear. Being a listener with few words makes him a decent friend. However, being secretive and keeping to oneself are rarely good things. 
My other concern is that after Da Pan arrived at Dijiang, many of our operators (and our Endministrator as well) began putting on significant amounts of weight... 
— Perlica </>
