[AUDIO LOG EXCERPT 1]
"AHEM— Talosian Calendar Year 15, ██ of ██. Day three after moving into the temporary shelters... QUIET, TORY! You're supposed to fix the chair, not bring down the house!
"Quit nagging already. And enough yapping about your fine studio at downtown Wrankwood. Hell, even I like a hot water bath and trashy movies to go along with it. But clean towels are a luxury now, okay?
"Oh, why don't you heard north, find 'Mr. Angels', take him out for a drink, and ask where his blighted kind hid the keys to the Cosmic Gate? —OF COURSE I KNOW IT DOESN'T EXIST. Where did your sense of humor go? Blown to pieces along with the stabilizer and the blighted Aggeloi?
"What am I doing? I'm making an audio log. Say, how about lending me that camcorder of yours? Your documentary project is on a temporary hold, right...? No? Fine. Blighted camera crew and their pride.
"Where was I again? Oh, yes. Today is Talosian Calendar Year 15—"

[AUDIO LOG EXCERPT 2]
"Dallied around for two weeks and still no news about the others. Murray, Ellie, Henry... I think they're still alive. I gotta keep thinking positive.
"We're one of the lucky ones. At least we got a roof here. The other shelters are jam-packed of people. They told me the war is over but there's no heading back to Terra. Meals are getting worse, too. Sheesh...
"...You're back? Wait. What the hell is that? A sword? You traded a can-o-food for a friggin' razor?! Are you friggin' nuts...?! Oh yeah, great! It killed a buggerloid! So what? Your backup camera almost got one of those buggers too —— KYAA! STOP! I'm sorry! It was my fault!
"You heard Ellie and Murray ended up at the shelters organized by the United Workers' HQ? Awesome. But I heard they have some serious hunger games going on at that place. I heard the UW is meeting up with the Corporate Security Council to talk about some 'shelter program'. Hah. This reminds me of the friggin' boring news on Terra. Never thought I would actually start reading these articles.
"Just ... try to stay here, Tory. Enough scavenging and trading already. Save your pitiful rations.
"And try to check your camcorder... Why? I don't know. I just ... just kinda feel we might get to use it again."

[AUDIO LOG EXCERPT III]
"Hmm... how long has it been? I hardly kept count. Maybe more than five months, maybe?
"Tory and I are now part of the Corporate Security Council entourage — Temporary, of course. We just tag along for a chance to get some worthy footage.
"So this entourage just got demolished yesterday. While beating the retreat, they ran into another equally ragtag band. Turned out to be peeps from the UW. Both sides got into some staring match for half a minute or so. Nobody said anything, but nobody reached for their weapons either. They just ... walked past each other. It felt so friggin' funny — but I couldn't even laugh during that encounter.
"We don't wanna fight, and they don't wanna fight either. But this war lasted more than five months. Why? Tory, got anything to say?
"Oh, right! Tory's out to get some footage. I told him to stick around but he won't listen. I kinda admire how he could still pick up his camcorder. I for one, got no idea why I'm recording anything and I don't feel like it anymore. Nobody's gonna watch our documentaries. But maybe Tory's right. Someone's gotta record the dumb crap and blightery that's going on.
"And oh yes, Tory's can-for-a-sword is still around. It's the reason why we're still breathing. I heard its OG owner was fighting too. Poor dude got un-alived because he refused to point his weapon at a pardner during the Aggeloi War. HAH! Now I'm laughing. Maybe I'm really mad.
"Crap! Crap! CRAP! It's starting again! Who's fighting who? I don't know. I never figured it out.
"...Blight this blightery. Where the hell is Tory?"

[VIDEO FOOTAGE (Blurry)]
"—HAHA! UP YOURS! We won, pardner! Our war friggin' drove the heavens MAD!! This is an Originium Catastrophe with CAPITAL C! The first of its kind on Talos-II! And we got ourselves some exclusive footage! LOOK, TORY!! It's exactly like what we got on Terra! See it, Tory?! You should be here, with me! Our reel will be nabbing tons of serious awards, Tory! NAME! Give our documentary a name, Tory! Lemme think... OH YES! Call it EFFIN' GLORIOUS MEMORY! That's super rad! We are SOOOOO totally gonna win those bling-bling trophies!
"OH! CHECK THAT OUT! That blighted tower is coming down — THERE! A perfect concluding shot! CONGRATULATIONS, HUMANITY!!"

CHIEF COMPLAINT 
Hit by an explosion. Multiple open and bleeding wounds. Shock after 45 minutes of intense pain. 

PRESENT ILLNESS 
Patient was conducting recon operations 5 klicks away from the site of the explosion but exercised personal initiative in changing the operational plan 45 minutes ago. Healthy. Denies chronic illnesses, past surgeries, and past blood transfusions. Oripathy negative.

Clouded consciousness, pallor, grimacing in pain

The city had many families. No one knew which of these families was the most friendly and harmonious. But everybody agreed that the Webers were the antithesis of peace. Rarely has there been a family with so many children and so many feuds. Only one Weber should be present in an area of sixty-four square klicks. If more Webers were present, the unfortunate land would soon witness violence and bloodshed.
Just last month, the eldest of the Weber children received a letter on the battlefield. After butchering the enemy who stood before him, he found his officer and applied for one-month of leave and embarked on a journey home. He crossed the woodlands and found his younger brother who was about to bury the axe into the elder Weber's head when the latter suddenly read the contents of the letter. The younger Weber tossed the axe, packed a few things, and joined his brother on a long journey.
Their sister was already waiting on a boat moored at the riverbank. The Weber boys were wary of the massive oar she wielded. Last time they were careless and woke up three days later.
Time was running out but they still had a lengthy journey ahead.
The three siblings faced a vast desert. When they were lost amongst the dunes of ever-changing shapes, a convoy arrived on time. The driver of the lead vehicle lowered the window and revealed a face they all despised and hated beyond all measure — Uncle Weber who lived miles away but never failed to show up and gloat at the family whenever they met difficulties.
"Hop on, brats," Uncle Weber offered a ride to the young Webers and ignored how they rolled their eyes. The other vehicles in the convoy honked and rushed them along. The frustrated cacophony undoubtedly hid a great number of Webers as well.
The convoy started off at once and left ephemeral trails upon the sands. They drove all through the night and day before finally arriving at the final stop. The lake was at peak water level, swollen by a storm that threw great waves crashing at its banks. Thankfully, the richest of their aunts owned a strong, majestic ship capable of accommodating every single Weber.
Aunt Weber the Captain proudly strolled the rolling decks as the ship tore through the storm and rode the waves, giving snorts of disdain to every Weber who failed to keep their stomach juices in, and grunts of contempt to the discolored Webers who held on to the railings for dear life. The tempest accompanied them throughout the journey, and all the Webers arrived at their homeland safely.
Everyone was shocked to see the Webers charging across the main avenue for the biggest hospital in town. There were so many of them that they covered the entire length of the road.
And the Webers finally gathered at the ward and surrounded a baby girl still in her wrappings. The infant weakly opened her eyes and looked at everyone present before closing them forever, untouched and untainted by the mundane affairs of the mortal world.
"Thank you for agreeing to see her one last time," the youngest of the Weber girls said softly as she cuddled the child whose body grew colder and colder.

DOCUMENT: A certain log that requires sufficient authority level 
According to reports by members of Operations Team Z7, Antal is exceptionally skilled in Originium Arts. His ability to cast the Arts far exceeds that of other operators in his cohort. When conducting a certain operation, Op Team Z7 members witnessed how Antal, in a crucial moment, positioned himself before the hostage. The operator used his Originium Arts to instantly disintegrate the greatsword swung by the attacking Landbreaker, and saved both himself and the hostage. 
It was an extremely intense moment. Antal would immediately lose his life if he failed to de-weaponize the attacker. However, he himself remained extremely calm throughout the entire incident. Since then, members of Op Team Z7 gained a deeper appreciation of Antal's abilities — Though he was known for being slow when it comes to sensing dangers in the environment or picking up changes in the emotions of other people, he was willing to risk his own life to save others. This revealed Operator Antal to be an extremely kind and courageous individual. 
Antal was remarkably humble when his teammates asked him about what he did. Antal replied that he did not perfectly wield his Originium Arts and failed to achieve his grandmother's level of expertise. He claimed the old lady could take apart and reassemble large metal machinery, while disintegrating a Landbreaker's weapon was the most he could do. Antal also mentioned that his grandmother crafted a small staff for him during his childhood to make up for his lack of power. 
"Your talent lies elsewhere — That is what my grandmother told me. And I have absolutely faith in her words." </>

-3675220694833104674:
The Sarkaz sat in a circle upon the soft, mushy snow. They had discussed the same problems multiple times for the past few months. Tactics for dealing with the ubiquitous Aggeloi, how many soldiers they should send to search and rescue the other races who were inept in fighting, and how they should live with the collapse of the Cosmic Gate and the fact that they would never see Kazdel again. 
The Aggeloi were like an unending flood. The swarming host covered every road, forced them out of the northern frontier outposts, and sent them on a desperate retreat. Once again they became roamers. A people without a future in sight, and without a way back to their homeworld. 
The sunlight reflecting off the great rings of the gas giant grew dimmer by the day. The walls became increasingly caked in blood, and food reserves ran low. The air grew stale and suffocating as fewer people had ideas to share. The Sarkaz remained silent, even when the Samifjod shared their goodwill. 
But this day was different, thought Fleming. Everyone must say something, so he broke the silence first. "Do we have a conclusion on that Feranmut tooth? Turn it into another Lifebone?" 
"I don't get it. Why give us a thing of such great value?" 
"Because we offered them crucial military support, maybe?" 
There was a brief pause. "But the Feranmut fell anyways." 
"Their Snowpriests mentioned a prophecy about us..." 
Confusion and uncertainty still saturated their words, but there was progress, however slow it was. Fleming tried to direct the flow of the discussion in the way he intended, and he did so by tweaking the topic. "There's no need to overthink it. This planetoid has a vile temper, one that forces people to work together if they wish to survive. And our relations with the Samifjod go way back. This isn't just about us. The others need the Lifebone as well. We must return north, win this war, and save more people... Our only consideration is how we can secure the blessing." 
When the "north" was mentioned, the Sarkaz fell silent once more. Nobody knew how long this war was going to last, and they were already tired and sick of it. 
Curses. A mistake. 
Fleming wiped the sweat from his forehead. The best sales pitch should never, ever reveal its bottom line so quickly. While he squeezed out a smile and frantically prepared another topic to revive the discussion, a Vampiress sitting furthest away, one that Fleming hardly knew, whose name even escaped his memories, took the lead. Elegantly she leaned against her thorny spear of blood red carmine, and spoke in her gentle voice that Fleming was familiar with. 
"Why? Don't any of you look forward to this? Tell me how many Sarkazian cities did we have back on Terra?" she purred as moldable blood glistened and rippled in mid-air as it slowly took the form of a city. "And now we have this distant planet filled with mysteries. Imagine, if you can, the possibility of us forging an era of peace, and think of the Talosian land and skies — I believe the time has come for us to raise our new home." 
"A floating city that cruises through the heavens upon the bones of the Feranmut. It must have its own style, and a powerful name." Fleming heard himself talk. 
"What about New Kazdel? Wait, that sounds too big... How about New Furnace?" 
"It would need a ring of permanent artillery and defensive works. Don't want no flying buggerloids striking from the skies!" 
The discussion turned solemn, somber, and stern... The people's faces revealed their longing for the new city that they would soon be building with their hands. The hesitation and uncertainty that reigned over the emotions of the Sarkaz were dispelled, and an unprecedented urge of impatience took their places. While the crowd clamored and argued, someone blurted out the word — "Seš'qa". A word without the prestige or greatness most envisioned, a place to serve a simple purpose. A midway stopping point between the road forward and the road home. 
But it was a beautiful word. Fleming juggled it on his tongue and mulled over the delicate tremors felt by his lower mandible, given force by the pulmonary exhalation required to lend voice to the word. An idea slowly crept into his mind — Why should the Sarkaz be a dark, brooding people with a penchant for violence and seek only warfare as their companion? No. The new city should be a theme park with a giant wheel ride, open-air bazaar, theaters, and every element of fun that could fit, and it did not matter if the element was not part of the Sarkazian past. 
The northern winds cut like razors, and it was the frigid cold that kept Fleming's mind in a state of crystalline clarity. His imaginations went wild. He had events in mind. "Lift-Off Day", "Open Day", "Parade of the Royal Courts" — festivals that the Sarkaz could use to gently land upon this planet, like a dandelion seed. 
This new city would not be blanketed in smoke from the funeral pyres for the fallen warriors. Instead, it would have something far more beautiful, like fireworks to bless its existence. 
It did not matter what the others thought. The Speaker on the other side of the Cosmic Gate should love this idea. She would be happy whenever someone mentions anything about explosives. 
Fleming would have many chances to prove his skills as a merchant. The next course of action would be to sell this idea.

<@profile.key>Three tolls of the bell sounded. One by one, the people at the gathering removed their hats and stepped forward to place fresh flowers into the cold coffin.
Some wept quietly, others bowed their heads in silence. Rozzan scanned the surroundings, but he didn't spot that familiar crimson figure anywhere.
The last of the Elder Wolves who survived the incident laid in the casket. He spent the rest of his days in pain. Though the Bonekrusher's haze ravaged his organs and their blades pierced his limbs, the Elder Wolf held on tightly to the swaddled young pup ... until he passed her into the arms of another boy...
"She's still not here..."
The words reached Rozzan. He gave a slow nod, then quietly passed the rest of the service over to another Elder.
He knew where to find her. Whenever she was upset, she'd lose herself in the training grounds and stay there until late into the night.
Rozzan watched the girl in silence. She noticed him too, but neither said a word. With one last fierce thrust, she drove her sword into the training dummy and collapsed to the ground. No one knew how long she had been pushing herself here.
"He's gone."
Rozzan approached Rossi where she lay gasping on the ground, his voice quiet and flat.
"I know... I know..."
Rossi pulled her hood down over her eyes, but her voice shook uncontrollably. Ever since she was old enough to understand, she had visited the wounded Old Wolf every single week so he could see that she was growing up strong and well. To her, he was the last living thread connecting her to those lost souls.
"You should have been there. He would have wanted you there."
"But ... it was because of me... He did it all for..."
Rozzan hoisted her up and slung her over his shoulder before she could finish, carrying her toward the courtyard where the funeral was being held.
"I can't face him ... it was all my fault... I don't want to..."
Rossi thrashed and bit against Rozzan's shoulder. Her nails scraped his skin, her teeth sank into his arm. Rozzan's expression didn't flicker. He just kept walking toward the funeral.
Soon, Rossi's strength gave out. She slumped against Rozzan's back, arms hanging limp.
"I didn't become the wolf the Pack could rely on..."
Rossi murmured, unsure if she was speaking to Rozzan, or to someone no longer there.
"I never learned to stand on my own. I couldn't lead anyone. I haven't done a single thing right... I didn't deserve their sacrifice..."
Rozzan came to a stop. The courtyard was empty now, save for the ashes of burnt offerings and a solitary coffin. Inside, the elder lay peacefully, covered in flowers.
"Every time you came to see him, he'd always pull me aside afterward to talk. Maybe age caught up to the wolf and he never remembered what he told me. Just kept ranting the same stories on and on."
Rozzan set Rossi down. He rested a hand on the edge of the coffin, gazing at his old friend.
"He'd always go on about the glory days, the few times we butted heads. But the details ... those kept changing. One day he was the one who messed up, the next it was me. The same story was told different every time. Only one thing he ever said never changed."
Rozzan reached over and ruffled Rossi's hair.
"Every single time, he'd say that saving you was the greatest thing he ever did."
Rossi lowered her head. She took off the pale pendant from around her neck, the one the elder had given her, and placed it among the flowers.
The coffin sealed. The young wolf never cried again.</>

<@profile.key>DOCUMENT: Investigation of an incident of fire 
CASE SUMMARY: Last night, a fire broke out in the second floor library of a residence on the border between the suburbs and the central district. Most of the furniture and retro-style clothing were damaged in the blaze. The fire was contained within the house. No casualties were reported. The book collection of the library escaped unscathed. 

1. Investigation of the site 
The library windows were locked from the inside. The locks appear undamaged. Two sets of fingerprints were collected. Footprints of a gardener responsible for regular pruning of the plants were found next to the garden. The fire started at the carved armoire. 

2. Investigation of surveillance records 
At around 2000 hours, the homeowner and his daughter had an extensive dialogue at the living room. At 2100 hours, both headed to the library. 

3. Witness testimonies 
Homeowner: "Apologies for troubling you into making this journey... But things are under control. People must burn the library once every a few centuries or so." 
Spouse of the homeowner: "My husband prepared that room before our girl was born. He wanted her to inherit that ancient culture, literature, and art, as well as to sow its seeds upon these new lands. I was hoping she could start a cultural restoration study group... The incident is a shame, really." 
Daughter of the homeowner: "Erm... We actually applied precision controls and barely suffered any losses! So why are we being inspected?" 
Governess: "I'm no longer giving meaningful instructions to the young mistress. Ballet and etiquette do not interest her. She is only willing to play the piano. The combined might of a hundred burdenbeasts could not force her to do something she doesn't like... What is she doing now? She's teaching me how to compose Neo-Talosian music and it's pretty interesting. Oh, I'm also learning electronic repairs from her. She has the engineer's knack, if you ask me." 

4. Post-incident handling 
After verifying various findings, we have ascertained that the incident was a private act of planned incineration. The responsible homeowner has been censured and fined. The incident does not need to be escalated to the community management department. 

5. Additional testimonies from the homeowner 
"'Fine,' I said, 'since you've chosen your path, we might as well burn the things.' She studied my face for quite a while. When we both realized neither of us was joking, she immediately started cheering. She said something about making a huge fireworks display and took out the contraptions she built... Maybe they're called drones. Anyway, these gadgets of hers could spew fire and ice." 
"I watched the library burn with her. Bright orange flame flickered behind the gaps of the door. I heard the wooden shelves crackle, burst, and split as the fire licked and consumed it." 
"I actually felt a certain degree of pain. The books in the house may not be antique relics, but I spent quite a tidy sum on acquiring this collection... I guess it can't be helped. It is the price I have to pay for spending years forcing her to go against her will. I have no choice but to demonstrate my stance." 
"But those two flying gadgets came buzzing out with the books. She giggled and said that we simply had different "tastes" and questioned on the necessity of destruction. She went on by saying that her preference for New Talos-II Wave literature does not mean she dislikes stories from further back. She even said that she had memorized those older tales." 
"So what was I saying again...? Apologies. I was too busy reminiscing about the smells given off by the fire. Oh, wait, I remember..." 
"I said to her, 'We can make this into a proper workshop. And make a drone for me if you have the time. The one that can light my cigars.'" </>

DOCUMENT: A Torn Manuscript 
The first mirror witnessed by a babe is usually the eyes of its mother. A mother would gaze at you and softly whisper these words: "Welcome to this world." You opened your eyes to look right back at her, with a focus shared by a navigator attempting to cross an ocean. Once the wet shimmers faded, you would see yourself reflected in her eyes. 
Powerful, weak, hateful, lovely, pure, tainted... You recognized the reflection in the mirror, a reflection of yourself. 
But what if your first mirror was not your mother? What if you opened your eyes before you uttered your first cry? The ocean around you swayed like a swinging cradle, and someone pressed against your fingers. It felt annoying but also calm. You did not know who this person was, but you peered through the turbid fluids, noticed another pair of blurry eyes, and saw your reflection in them. At that very moment, something faster than a bolt of lightning struck through your soul. 
He was born with you. You were the closest friends, yet you always fought and argued. You could not help but peer into his eyes to look at your own reflections... He was the rule and the control by which you were measured against, and the very conduit by which you fed from the world. He, on the other hand, relied upon you, respected you, and envied you. The days passed and your reflection within his eyes grew ever more perfect. 
Then one day it came. The first crack appeared in the mirror. The cracks spread, and the mirror shattered. Your image was gone. The storm descended, the fates murmured, and the oceans drove back into the deep. You gained a scar that would never heal, lost half of your soul, and were forced to raise your weapon against him. It was the only way with which you could pierce the hatred that burned deeper than love and restore what was broken to completion. 
And that moment, you still had not realized — 
— that you were his first mirror. 

DOCUMENT: A Faded News Cutting 
Landbreakers Raid Towns - Seš'qa Planning to Create an Anti-Witchcraft Organization 
The floating city traitor and deserter Jakub Meissen and the Landbreaker raiders he led have recently become a major security threat to the Civilization Band. Jakub's forces have occupied and transformed an Originium farm into their base of operations, sending out raider groups to spread more Originium and raid. 
Just two nights prior, a town at the Band Fringes was attacked by raiders led by a Vampire serving as Jakub's lieutenant. The town, situated at an area not yet claimed by Talosian factions, was poorly defended. However, another Vampire, who hailed from Seš'qa, played a pivotal role in thwarting the raid. Armed with knowledge of Sarkazian witchcraft, the Vampire defender sabotaged the raiders' military hardware and ran his weapon through the chest of the raid leader, forcing the latter to call for retreat. Currently, the raider leader has gone into hiding and Seš'qa is maintaining constant vigilance to track him down. 
Seš'qa regarded Jakub's betrayal as its responsibility. The latest news revealed that the leadership of the floating city is planning to create an organization dedicated to fighting crimes involving Sarkazian witchcraft and apprehending the traitors.

He has joined the Specialist Tech Division as an independent, with recommendations from Operator Chen Qianyu and a letter of authentication from HAS. We also respected his personal wishes and granted him partial authority levels for canteen access. 

Da Pan provided an incredibly chaotic CV. His verifiable work experiences include: owner of hot pot eatery, LA-ME-DA (literal translation: Spicily Huge); tianshi at HAS; electrician; carpenter; machinist; and background extra in Heyi Quan: Zailin (literal translation: Fist of Combined Will: Revisited). 
Two of his past experiences cannot be verified. The first was a brief stint of driving taxis at Simonch. We failed to find any commercial driving license or records for Da Pan in the said city. When I pointed out this finding, the Ursus' maw cracked into a 70-degree smile and he applied a rather powerful slap on my mechanical chassis. The second would be "friendly assists and support". Da Pan claims he part-timed as an ornamental burdenbeast stand-in for three days at La Fantoma. By the time I realized that I had been misled into an engrossing dialog about unlicensed taxi driving and ornamental burdenbeasts, we had already been talking for four hours — and I had neglected to ask Da Pan about the experiences that he should remember best: his time as a tianshi at HAS. 
While verifying his experiences in HAS, Da Pan became visibly downcast and displeased. But he quickly resumed his smile and deflected the topic with a casual joke. Then he showed me a friendly group photo of him and other ornamental burdenbeasts. I could obviously tell that he was trying to avoid talking about his disagreeable past with other Tianshi, but this is not a negative consideration for Endfield. Since Da Pan is still affected by the Science Station incident, it proves that he remains, deep inside, a HAS tianshi who upholds a strong sense of principles, responsibilities, and duty. 
— Martin Marvin Malen, Assistant, HR Division, Endfield Industries</>

-3397854095914037297:
I remember our last encounter with the "Angel". It was one hundred days ago. It was February. It was our last sweep for potential cave-ins caused by Ankhorfalls. The Aggelos appeared without warning at the back of the team just as we approached the edge of a sinkhole. Old Liu was the first to get hit. His alarm failed to alert him and only started shrieking when the enemy disabled his Tianshi apparatus. That was how we learned of the threat. Tobin reacted quickly. He immediately fired at the Aggelos's abdomen. It howled and then swung its razor-sharp tail. Tobin and Kachinsky could not evade but took the hit for me. They bought me an opportunity to unload my last bullet. The Aggelos collapsed in pain. Maybe. People say the Aggeloi do not feel anything. Not even pain — This blightery is unfair. 
I never saw the Aggelos again after that. 
The war finally ended. 

The investiture was held at our base near the North. They organized it to praise and award the soldiers who performed admirably. As the only survival of Outpost 158, I walked in the middle of the column of awardees, flanked front, back, left, and right by veterans like me. We're all war heroes now, dressed in brand new uniforms fitting for the investiture. Speaking of uniforms, the last time I got a new outfit was during my first arrival at Talos-II. The local committee of the frontiers organized a mass marriage to uphold the spirit of the Black Hole Protocol. Fifty-two pairs of newlyweds from Yan, Ursus, Victoria ... settling down and starting families in this foreign world. I was one of them. I was young but crossing that Gate drained every ounce of courage out of me. Old Liu was young too. Just passed the Tianshi admission exams and so proud of himself. He took my hand and told me to have no fear. Liu promised that we would, together, overcome every obstacle of this world and build our new home upon this planet. 
And so I marched alone down the lengthy path towards the investiture platform. The cheering of the crowd was passionate, but distant. I counted the awardees and could not even finish. 
The war finally ended. 

The aftermath of the war was worse than we thought. Refugees from the north kept coming in. They brought news that "everything we built was gone". Every receiving area was packed of them. Sprawling industrial parks and factory plants from more than ten years ago are now replaced by drab, ashen temporary shelters. Riots quickly followed. Workers fought corporate soldiers in Development Zone 2. They were one step away from full out war. News of such unrest also fanned the unrest within the Tianshi Bureau. Some Tianshi started labeling factions as "Protocolites" and "Anti-Protocolites" and seemed eager to introduce hostilities amidst our ranks. Tianshi Ruan, one of Old Liu's classmate, petitioned the Bureau multiple times, hoping that they would issue an official statement to quell the increasingly antagonistic atmosphere. All he received was the same rebuke: "True strength lies in maintaining our unwavering neutrality." Some even tried to contact Dijiang that continued to cruise in orbit, but even Endfield Industries stayed silent. Only the attack on Hongshan-1 Mass Driver made them realize that the facade of neutrality can no longer disguise the long festering rifts amongst ourselves. 
It just another day, but a group of farmers barged into the Hongshan-1 power supply facilities. Though quickly apprehended and confined by the Tianshi, the farmers barked loudly at us: "Why won't you fix that Cosmic Gate! Why won't you send us home with this mass driver?" The Tianshi paid them no heed and kept them behind bars. One of the arrested farmers was a Feline girl less than ten years of age. She asked her father: "Papa, why are we going home? I thought we have a home at this place." Her father could not give her an answer. 
Then again, how are we supposed to tell her that this massive "refugee camp" was her home? How are we supposed to explain why we left Terra and stepped onto this planet in the first place? Many of us could hardly remember the reasons. 
We found ourselves trapped behind a prison of our own making. 
The war finally ended. 

There was a minor disturbance during noon. It was deliberately started it to distract the patrolling Tianshi. We came out of hiding from the vehicles and crossed the boundary line. A young security Tianshi guarded the final pass out of Hongshan. Our gazes crossed as I loaded a round into the firing chamber. The Tianshi did not activate his alarm or raise his Arts Unit. 
"I'm a humble disciple of Tianshi Ruan, and I've been waiting for a while," his words brought me out of my startled stupor. 
"What of Tianshi Ruan himself?" 
"My mentor instructed that the departure is best done in groups. He left before any of you. If finding a new home is your wish, he will do his best to see it fulfilled." 
He pushed a pass of emerald bamboo into my hand as he spoke. "Qingbo" was the word inscribed upon it. 
"Exit the city, then make for the mountains. He shall meet you there." 
The war finally ended.

My combat style? It's based on the arrays that my Father taught me combined with Yinglung tactics. 
Father said that arrays operate on the principle of "change". The array gives the wielder momentum, and moves with the wielder as well. No array should be unchanging or permanent. An array is only complete when the wielder becomes part of it. 
Father brought me to many places when I was a girl. Sometimes we rode logs down rivers. Sometimes we climbed really tall trees. And when we got tired, we'd just lie down on the grass to gaze at the stars... Father taught me their positions and the shapes of the constellations. I later learned that none of this was just a "game". He used a subtle yet engaging way to teach me his knowledge of arrays and the cycles of all sorts of entities. 
The Yinglungs, however, taught me the meaning of "permanence", and how to remain unmoving in the midst of a storm. The Yinglung tactic relies primarily on "momentum" to create an unstoppable force. Different tactics are used against different threats. Yet it does not matter if we fought with swordmancy, spearmancy, or with our formations and arrays. Every Yinglung stuck to their post and focused on unleashing the momentous strike to obliterate the foe. 
I tried integrating Yinglung tactics with my Father's arrays. The former focuses on the team, the entire battlefield, and complementing each other's moves, like how my triplex cannon function as a single unit. My Father's arrays focus on flexibility and change. Combining these two approaches was difficult and troubled me for quite some time... 
But then I revisited the place where Father and I used to play. I saw how falling leaves passed through river rapids, how fowlbeasts perched at the end of long branches swung with the wind, and how the constellations never stopped yet somehow retained their shapes — Then I suddenly understood what Father used to say. I am the key. I must be part of the formation, the fourth piece of the array. 
I am the knot and pivot by which the array changes, the variable element that fills the tactical gap. Once I learned the lesson, I incorporated myself into the array. With my jade slip I positioned the triplex cannon and adjusted its firepower until it felt like an extension of my arm and leg. Only then did I master its use. 
My Originium Arts focus more on the "flow" of energy to create an equilibrium of "change" and "permanence". In a way, my Arts are similar to those wielded by Operator Gilberta. She shared a few tips about Arts casting with me. Operator Arclight also wielded electrical currents with beautiful elegance and mastery, and so I asked her for advice as well. She responded with a phrase: "Feel it." Indeed, Dijiang is a gathering of incredibly talented and skilled individuals and offers plenty of learning opportunities, like Operator Last Rite with her astronomical strength and Operator Pogranichnik with his unparalleled knowledge of military formations... I hope my stay aboard Dijiang will give me a chance to improve my own skills and study the strengths of every school... 
I'm also trying to compile these lessons into a book. Other Yinglungs trying to master the arrays and heavy cannons can use it for reference. I hope these writings can provide them with assistance.

<@profile.key>Neo Tsukushi Business School News - Special Edition 
On the eve of the graduation ceremony, our reporter sat down with top graduate Shiba Momiji for an exclusive interview. 
"Miss Momiji, you've maintained the top GPA in your major for four years straight and won two gold medals in the TGCC Youth Business Competition. What has kept you so driven all this time?" 
Shiba Momiji smiled and replied, "It's just how I do things. Or maybe it's the way my mother taught me to approach life ever since I was little." 
Shiba Momiji interned at several top-tier TGCC companies. Her experiences included an on-site rotation at the headquarters of Shinozu Trading, as well as contributing to a business proposal for TGCC's logistics coordination system. Her key optimization ideas for the risk assessment model received glowing feedback from company leaders. Yet when asked about the achievement she's most proud of over the past four years, she spoke fondly of her work with the volunteer group Firefly Light. 
"I've always believed that the true value of business and management lies not only in profit, but also in how we support one another. Firefly Light taught me how to stretch limited resources to help as many people as possible." 
When asked about future plans: "Your mother runs Shiba Trading as its CEO. Many assume you'll follow in her footsteps, especially since you've never publicly expressed other ambitions. With graduation just around the corner, can you share your plans?" 
Shiba Momiji simply shook her head and grinned, "I've made up my mind. But ... you'll have to wait a little longer to find out." 

A Self-Recommendation Letter 
Dear HR Team at Endfield Industries, 
My name is Momiji Shiba, a student at the Neo Tsukushi Business School. I am writing to express my interest in joining Endfield Industries in a position focused on resource management and personnel coordination. 
Though I do not come from a technical or combat background, I specialize in logistics, coordination, and on-site problem-solving. I firmly believe these skills can make a meaningful contribution. I am ready to undergo any required training or evaluation and am willing to take on front-line responsibilities if needed. My goal is to be a dependable team member who helps others work more safely and efficiently. 
Thank you for your time and consideration. I have attached my resume, transcript, internship records, and project examples from past competitions. I look forward to hearing from you! 

Shiba Momiji</>

The cleric named "Sessionite" thus entered the wildlands.
And he arrived at an abandoned village. The creek had long dried up and the soil was cracked.
And the Fortes, suffering hunger and thirst, asked him for salvation.
"You need knowledge that will lead you to where the water flows and the thick grasses grow."
"I shall teach you how to read these lands."
And so his hand gleamed with the light of the Originium Network,
And he imparted upon them knowledge that came from those from afar.
After seven days and seven nights,
The enlightened Fortes learned how to dig a water well in the barrens,
And thus the water flowed and the grasses grew forever more.

The cleric named "Resurgonite" thus entered the wildlands.
And he arrived at an abandoned village. The creek had long dried up and the soil was cracked.
And the Fortes, suffering hunger and thirst, asked him for salvation.
"You need strength to retake the watering hole that you once called yours."
"I shall grant you weapons to protect your kin."
And then he removed the guns he carried on his back,
And together with the relics of the old, he gave them to the Fortes he met.
After seven days and seven nights,
The armed Fortes drove the Landbreakers that occupied the upper flows of the river and chased them out of these lands,
And thus the water flowed and the grasses grew forever more.

The cleric named "Veritarite" thus entered the wildlands.
And he arrived at an abandoned village. The creek had long dried up and the soil was cracked.
And the Fortes, suffering hunger and thirst, asked him for salvation.
"You must converge your faith as one, and pray for a rain of abundance."
"I shall be with you, and lead you to wait for the destined season of rain."
And then he codified the Law and the commandments, and taught them unity and forbearance,
And he patiently encouraged every Forte whose despair was great in their hearts, and gave them peace and hope.
After seven days and seven nights,
A torrent of life-giving rain fell for the persevering Fortes,
And thus the water flowed and the grasses grew forever more.

If you are the thirsty Forte,
Which of these clerics' teachings will you accept?

— The Parable of the Three Clerics, engraved at one corner of the Sanctilamina Cathedralis Tranquillae

<@profile.key>"How long are you gonna stay this time? You coming home?" 
"...A day. And nah." 
"Just a day? Then never mind ... sigh. Well, a couple of days ago, Rossi was whining again, saying she thinks you'll pull the same stunt this year — you know, 'the gift arrives, but the brother doesn't.' Come on, even if you're not planning to come home, you could at least find time to see her once in a while." 
"It's already been what, over half a year? Since you two last met up at Tommaso's place." 
"I still need to take care of a few things. Once it's done..." 
"Stop right there! That's what you said last time! Then you ran off to the frontier, saying you had to clean up someone's mess..." 
"Gosh, I don't get you young folks. How do you always have so much to do?" 
"Hey, if I were you, no matter how swamped I was, I'd still swing by more to check in on my little sis. She's a kid! Every other kid her age in the clan's doted on by their families all day every day..." 
"You're her family too." 
"Well, yeah — Wait! No, don't try to spin this on me... I get you've got your own things going on. But listen, as someone who's been there — whenever I see little Rossi, I can't help but think of my own little girl... Biggest regret of my life? Not being there for her when I still had the chance." 
"Just hear me out, Catello... Life's short, don't do things you'll end up regretting." 
"I hear you. Uncle Rust."  
"Rossi knows I'm back today." 
"WHAT? No way!" 
"Then why would she run off to the hunting grounds first thing in the morning with the Louis twins? Unless..." 
"Uh-huh. Exactly." 
"Argh... You two really are true Lupus. So stubborn and so damn alike ... it's scary." 
"Alright, alright. Do whatever you like! But if you're always absent, aren't you worried something might go wrong?" 
"I was gonna keep it from you for Rossi's sake ... but looks like you need to hear it. Six months ago, she got herself into serious trouble — stuck her neck out for Old Bart and his men, and ended up on the Shadowskull's hit list. I remember it clear as day. Fourteen of them showed up, each nastier than the last. If Tommaso hadn't pulled some strings and brought in Capone's Fangs, we probably wouldn't have even made it out of the black market alive..." 
"..." 
"Worried now, huh?" 
"Nope. I was just wondering how Rossi found out I was heading north. It was you, wasn't it?" 
"Oh! Um, heh ... well ... yeah, I might've let that slip ... wasn't on purpose though..." 
"Ahem, anyway! I checked your guns! They're as good as new! Just ease up on those custom rounds of yours. No barrel's gonna last with the way you burn through them..." 
"Got it." 
"And ... there were actually fifteen of them." 
"Huh?" 
"Alright, see you around." 
— Audio log from Howlfire Gunsmiths</>

A formal challenge to all modern "avant garde" artists of Talos-II

To those who call themselves the great masters of the "avant garde":
How are you doing? I'm specifically talking to those who spraypaint shapes on the walls of ruins, the howlers of underground dive bars in La Fantoma, and anyone who fantasized about having a hand in creating "unprecedented" works of art.
I gotta tell you a brutal truth. At least 90% of your so-called "avant garde" art are actually dug out from the ancient heaps known as Terran history.
La Fantoma got a new rapper brand? After viewing ten live recordings from the most classic Obsidian Festivals at Siesta, these so-called neo-rappers got NOTHING on the giant known to us as "Emperor"! They made ZERO innovations on the beats, rhyme, and rhythm. [LINK NO LONGER VALID] 
Hundred-Strong Graffiti of the Asphalt Roundabout? From what I unearthed, these giant graffiti were past-tense in the Ursus factories of Terra. The Infected crew were already creating mega-graffiti at their barracks and production floors. [ATTACHMENT NOT FOUND]
Neo-Youth Film Festival of New Wrankwood? Hah. That's an even bigger joke. The Talosian free city can't even come up with their own name and just took something from the Terran city of Wrankwood.
So where the hell can we find true avant garde art of Talos-II?
If you want novelty and innovation, I'll tell you what it means to be truly avant garde.
I've unearthed a video about the Endfield Protocol-Originium Technology (Protorig Tech). [Author has set the video to pay per view]
Many might be confused about the Protorig Tech I mentioned. But you know that art cannot be fully detached from industrial tech. Derivative works of aesthetics based on Terran technology will end up like those sorry examples I listed above. We will never free ourselves from the label of Terran culture!
But Protorig Tech is the most "avant garde" and "coolest" innovation that happens to be Talos-exclusive, isn't it? It completely shattered our understanding of spatial dimensions, but why haven't I seen any artist using them as a fount for artistic creation?
Avant garde isn't about going through your trash or pasting new labels on old antiques.
So if you're fumbling around with stuff that your grandparents had fun with, STAAHHHP calling yourself "avant garde".

<@profile.key>DOCUMENT: A funeral speech 
It was an ordinary morning, like all the other mornings that HAS had received before. But when the sunlight poured into the office, my husband had already passed away in his dreams. 
He committed his entire life to the Hongshan Academy of Sciences — Naturally there was a time when I hated it. Whenever I stepped into the corridors to deliver his meal, I felt only annoyance when I heard the all-knowing Tianshi debate each other. I didn't care if they were trying to get permanent tenure, jostling for higher positions, or really trying to get people fed. I didn't want to know why they were creating stacks of paper with no actual benefits to the environment. None of these mattered to me. 
I didn't understand why they would neglect their own lives just so others could survive and live theirs. It felt as though "survival" was a canon rule of the Academy, or an abstract concept. Perhaps their entire philosophy, career, and even existence was just part of this obsession of theirs. 
............ 
With my own hands I buried my daughter's dress at this public cemetery many years ago. She was one of the 113 who left us in the early days of the Wuling Science Station. 
...My husband and I had not talked for years. When I learned that my darling girl's vital signs ceased, he was carrying out the consecutive voting process with the old Tianshi. He only called me after three days. I was in tears when I asked why we couldn't bring the children's remains back home. He only told me it was impossible. At that time, the only wish on my mind was to strap myself with explosives and take my husband and those old academicians to the grave — that is ... until two incredibly young Tianshi opposed the vote. One was Viceroy Zhuang, and the other was an Ursus. The latter made quite a scene at HAS and soon left Hongshan after submitting his resignation. 
I thought the young lad, having expressed his disagreements in such a physical manner, wouldn't attend the funeral. But I saw him before everyone gathered here. He grew up and matured. He came quietly, and left just as quietly. He shared no words with anyone ... and left nothing but a jar of Mrs. Pepper. 
And now with my hands I buried my husband. I still detest HAS for having devoured my entire family. Yet I know that he ... that child, and every young Tianshi standing here with us whom my late husband had mentored, you have nothing but love for the Academy. 
At least he had flowers and his favorite hot sauce by his side when he left us. 

FILE: Repaired audio log 
"Dozens of hours had passed. Unfortunately, we have picked up no vital signs in the vicinity of the Very Large Rift. Since we have a unanimous consensus, we shall act upon the decision and cease all SAR operations." 
"Objection! I'm not going to argue whose proposal it was and how it ended up this way! But at least have the common decency to bring our people out, dead or alive! How could we even face their families after this?! Zhuang Fangyi, don't you dare side with them!" 
"Calm down and let me say something. Professor Huang... I believe Tianshi Pan is right. Giving up right now goes against the collective as well as individual spirit espoused by the HAS. I recommend continuing our SAR efforts." 
"Zhuang, I couldn't believe you actually agreed with Tianshi Pan on something, but this isn't the moment or place... Listen to us. This isn't giving up. We simply couldn't get it done. As Tianshi, you should use the balance of reason and understand this is us weighing the living against the dead. Now, get back to your seats." 
"Couldn't get it done?! Then think of something to get it done!" 
"Not everyone is like you, Pan Yuan..." 
"[Yanese expletive]." </>

<@profile.key>Regular Work Report for Operators Under the Endministrator 
REPORTED BY: Laevatain 

I escorted the messenger to this volcanic basin. Molten lava flowed through the ground beneath our feet, heating the rain and creek, causing the earth to froth and bubble endlessly. The monitoring station stood right atop this "cauldron of living soup". 
This place is extremely poor in Originium. Resident scientists rely on geothermal heat to cook food. A ration tin can be cooked through simply by burying it in the dirt for an hour. They even have "pocket stews": a liquid stock and other ingredients sealed in a food-grade bag — after quick cooking, you can just tear it open with your teeth. I got a face full of hot stew once, and it felt like I was on fire. 
When I had my first meal, the scientist taught me to sing their "ritual" chant: "May your soup never spill, and may your flame never die." 
I sang the chant with him. It was the first time I received a stranger's blessing on Talos-II. 
— Sent from Monitoring Station 34 

As the Operator closest to the incident and the most capable emergency responder, I was ordered to reach the UWST base not marked on the map with the greatest speed I could muster. 
The issue was not complicated. Just an unexpected blast furnace malfunction, shutdown, and loss of power. I spent a bit of my powers and helped them re-ignite the core. Temperature returned to operational levels and the system was restored. The crisis was temporarily averted. 
Their "names" left quite an impression on me. The place was a secret base in the frigid lands of █████, usually referred to by its unique beacon code. Everyone there was forbidden from using their real names or any self-chosen codenames; only the "assigned" name was allowed. 
My temporary name here was "Olga Randall". I was told there were three others before me with the same name, and it's likely that the next replacement actuary sent here will also take on this name. 
It was a strange experience. I was just a temporary user of the name "Olga Randall". It felt similar to the memory fragments swimming in my mind. Neither the name nor the fragments were truly mine, but at that very moment, they were all part of me. 
— Sent from UWST Beacon DAU.14 

After eliminating the Aggelos camping in the freight station, I reopened the gate that had kept the tunnel sealed for quite a while. 
They maintained a low gravity environment within the tunnels. Refugees, trapped here for months, floated their way to the exit, trembling and struggling as they left the place. They must relearn how to walk and run under the ponderous influence of gravity. 
But there was a little girl who floated within the tunnels and danced for a bit before leaving the place. She told me it was how she kept herself calm and sane when they were trapped in this place. 
I memorized her dance, a comforting yet powerful routine of rhythms. If you want, I can show it to you and let you have a go once I head back. The moves aren't hard. It's all about the breathing and the rhythms. 
— Sent from freight nexus MC-20 

I've made plenty of new memories during this time. I still remember that you're chasing after your own memories as well. I found a few places related to the old "you". Seek me out if you're interested. 
— Emergency message, sent from Contact Point 084A </>

<@profile.key>In a time when most Landbreakers are seen as "destroyers of order", the Pack stands out as an anomaly. They value order and hold a peaceful attitude toward the Civilization Band. Even now, they cling to certain old traditions, such as strong familial bonds and a deep respect for unity. 
That very difference only fueled the long-standing feud between them and their rivals, the Bonekrushers. Over ten years ago, the Bonekrushers struck with a vicious ambush, shattering the Pack when they were at their weakest — just after the death of their Alpharion. 
Wulfgard and his younger sister survived the attack, but they refused to speak of what truly happened. 
Wulfgard then left the Pack a few years after his coming-of-age ceremony, keeping in touch with only a few trusted friends and his sister. 
No one ever knew why he left. He stayed silent, just like he did about the attack. 
Later, he approached Endfield and proposed a partnership. He eventually joined the Specialist Tech Division as an operator. 
Someone once asked why he chose Endfield. 
At first, he was silent. Then, with startling honesty, he answered: 
"I want another future for the Pack... and Endfield holds the possibility of making it real." 
Wulfgard spoke candidly of the Pack's struggles. His steady resolve and honest intent opened doors. 
So it made perfect sense when he became an operator. As he put it, he had a duty — to prove the Pack's worth and to repay Endfield's trust in him. 
Since then, he's become a quiet but reliable presence on many tough and dangerous missions. 
Operators who once held deep prejudice against the Landbreakers began to change their views — thanks to Wulfgard. 
Then, opinions shifted once more after the arrival of his sister — Operator Rossi. But that's a story for another time...</>

-1718872697410827340: First, we are certain that the outsider who made these notes was remarkably intelligent. This observant individual keenly identified the feature of the Marker Stone construction project that most warrants investigation: its deep integration with the aquatic environment. The entire Marker Stone and its nearby facilities are actually arranged in a way that resembles a multi-tiered terrace. We can divide this "terrace" into three portions based on the installation's purpose of suppressing the Very Large Rift (VLR): (1) the resistance portion; (2) the buffer portion; and (3) the central processing portion. The "resistance portion" naturally refers to the Marker Stone itself, a gigantic Tianshi Pillar with Xiranite coursing through it. This portion is capable of creating a boundary that contains the Blight. The "buffer portion", as the repair personnel's memo suggests, would be the water stored within the Reservoir Station. The buffer essentially helps to buy Wuling time for activating its emergency measures. If something were to happen to the resistance portion, the affected body of water would be directed to the third portion, namely the central processing portion. This portion has active Xiranite particles scattered within it (which you probably could not observe directly in the Marker Stone area), allowing it to immediately treat Blight-affected water. In addition to the designs of these three portions, the Marker Stone is also furnished with underwater defenses. The Aggeloi of Wuling tend to lurk within water bodies. To prevent the Marker Stone from being damaged, the installation also boasts a comprehensive suite of aquatic defenses (unfortunately, this is also not directly observable from your perspective). A great deal of effort must have been invested to construct this terraced installation. From the data that Hongshan Academy of Sciences (HAS) synced with us, we have learned how the Wulingers prepared for the construction of the Marker Stone in the Year 143. They started by excavating a Blight-breaking belt before moving on to sealing the local aquifers and furnishing the area with underwater defenses to defeat Aggelos attacks. Marker Stone construction was completed with incredible speed.

<@profile.key>LOG ID: 0000000 
Hoo... This message is for me (at some point in the future) and the person who could hear these logs. 
After leaving the Woods, she once said, "Try recording special and unique moments in your life. It may help you anchor yourself in the world." 
Till now, I don't know if I really understood what she meant. And I'm unsure what type moment can be considered "special and unique"... So, I might as well record everything that I think is worth remembering. 

LOG ID: 0000001 
...This is my first time leaving Rhodes Island and stepping on the land of Talos-II. It's more spacious and open than what the maps and panoramic holograms suggested... There are also plenty of things I have not yet seen in her memories. Although this place is quite different from Terra, the people and buildings feel distant yet familiar at the same time... It's so strange... 
But if possible, I really want to see and experience the local snow... They say there are snowy mountains in the north and the central part of the Band. The north seems closer, so I guess I'll head over there first. 

LOG ID: 0000009 
...Today I arrived at a snowcapped mountain in the north. I felt right at home in this polar landscape. Everything, including the hexagonal columnar snowflakes and the veil-like aurora, felt really familiar to me... Before I forget, I ran into a huge blizzard when I made my way down the mountain. Two Fortes dressed like messengers were almost trapped in a nearby Blight. I used my snowboard to pull one of them to safety. The other was saved by a fully armed Perro. We escorted them to a safe place in a timely fashion... I later learned that the Perro is a volunteer with the Northern Corridor Rescue Union. They are planning to establish a professional SAR team. That Perro also left me a business card when we said goodbye. He said I behaved with calmness and reason despite my lack of professional training, even choosing the best rescue measures possible. Then he asked if I'd be interested in joining his outfit... 
Truth be told, when I pulled that messenger to safety, I did feel ... a kind of ecstasy and joy I had never experienced before. It became a calling I couldn't ignore, and I even wanted to do more. 

LOG ID: 0000010 
I thought about giving it a shot, so I called the Perro named Chris. I told him I want to be an SAR teammate. 
I am doing this for myself. The sunshine after the blizzard was also especially bright. I want to see that again. </>

<@profile.key>Raindrops beaded along the edge of Gilberta's umbrella, each droplet swelling with borrowed weight before surrendering to gravity. Before one could shatter against the ground, she caught it midair with a flick of the Arts and let it balance on her fingertip. 
This was her first journey beyond Rhodes Island. The skies were always a weeping steel. She walked unhurried, pausing whenever she felt like it. 
Her gaze drifted between the distant horizon and the letter in hand - Warfarin's assignment, her first duty as a Talos-II Messenger.
She'd lingered too long on the road watching burdenbeasts amble, flying wing-to-wing with fowlbeasts, even letting raindrops on her umbrella's edge steal her attention. 
Warfarin never set her a delivery deadline. Just an encouragement: "Go see the world." 
Gilberta understood Warfarin's message: she needed to deepen her bond with this planet before answering her calling. It was something she genuinely wanted to do as well. 
But where to next? Her eyes wandered. A strange glow shimmered at the foot of a mountain. Wild creatures circled near a tower on the open plain. A breeze stirred the curtain at a distant mail depot. Every sight pulled her forward. 
"Take it slow, I've got plenty of time," Gilberta thought to herself as she looked at the letter sealed with the crest of an industrial company. 
"Just a little longer. I'll be there." 
She then flicked the raindrop into the stream before her. As the skies cleared, the Messenger closed her umbrella and resumed with her journey.</>

<@profile.key>Operator Chen Qianyu was a native of Hongshan City and once served at the Wuling Scientific Developmental District. Supervisor Perlica later recruited her, via a private channel, to Endfield Industries. She is now a core member of the Crisis Team. Given her outstanding capabilities and mobility, Operator Chen Qianyu is an indispensable component of the Team. 

Those seeking to join Endfield have demonstrated a wide range of literary skills when describing their motives. However, the HR Division has yet to establish basic standards for reviewing the [Personal Motivations] section. If this section were completed in a manner that is too curt and/or straightforward, I will ask the operator to re-write their motivations in a style that they are comfortable with. However, despite being given five standard days to revise this section, Operator Chen Qianyu still persisted in writing: "I just wanna join. It's fate." Reading this, I realized the need to reflect upon our current review standards and establish a new framework, while paying extra attention to the two blades that Operator Chen Qianyu placed on my table (though she claimed that she did not do so to threaten me). 
Operator Chen Qianyu's inner thoughts and feelings are not as casual as she makes them out to be. Taking into consideration of her relatively rich past experiences, it is obvious that the extremely brief and terse description of her personal motives was a conclusion she arrived at after an extended period of self-contemplation. 
Additionally, I also realized that Operator Chen Qianyu's recruitment has been specifically approved by Supervisor Perlica. From my readings, the recent years have been a period where our Supervisor exhibited emotional fluctuations. The operator managed to solve many potential issues by offering much needed stability and support. 
Most importantly, I may have neglected how the simple line: "I just wanna join. It's fate." is actually congruent to the inner logic of the Endfield strategic objectives. In other words, these words could be seen as an alternate interpretation of the "Unity in Purpose" approach in partnership espoused by our Endministrator, which I also have in my records. Perhaps we now have an explanation capable of satisfying all parties involved in this review. 
— Martin Marvin Malen, Assistant, HR Division, Endfield Industries</>

Dear Klamath Bob:
I received your message. Though I desire to have this discussion in person, my convoy must depart for the Northern Front in 10 hours. It was with some hesitation that I decided to pen this reply. Do be aware that I will have difficulty contacting you via conventional comm devices once the convoy sets off.
I understand your concerns and I'm very well aware of the sadness and disappointment experienced by your team. As your mentor, you must understand that my decision was nothing personal and must cater to the bigger picture. My opinions alone would not sway the strategies of our marketing department. The fact that your technical blueprints earned no small amount of approval is a testament to the outstanding performance of your designs. You should be confident about that.
Just two months ago, I was shocked when engineers from the fringe tech department released a working example of a miniaturized centrifugal Originium generator. It shattered the theoretical limits of energy conversion ratios for such devices and would certainly usher in the next revolutionary change for the very foundations of power generation. Even I would have brushed it off as mere hypothetical fantasy just 12 months ago but the truth proved otherwise. I was trapped in a comfort zone that blinded me from the scientific advancements that was within our reach.
So, don't let this setback dishearten you or keep you from learning. You are young and your choices are many. Though conventional Originium power generation remains a field with great potential, science and technology are always changing. It is difficult to accept failure, especially after so many years of hard work. But remember that you are an engineer. Do not let emotions affect your objectivity.
Based on my own experiences, there will be a protracted period of time before the new tech becomes fully adopted. Stories from the Age of Terra often describe noisy old engines with abysmal Originium energy conversion ratios. Despite their poor performance, these engines offered advantages that the latest generators could not hope to provide — reliability and ease of maintenance. The world still has a place for the legacy workhorses and it will be long until they are completely phased out.
Regardless of what I've said, your product design remains an outstanding work of engineering. I have faith that you and your team will quickly find a new direction.
I look forward to hearing more about your progress in the future.

Your friend and mentor,
Willem Sinclair

NAME: Mi Fu 
REGION OF ORIGIN: Wuling 
WORK EXPERIENCE: 3 years 
CURRENT POSITION: Wuling Watchguard 
PROPOSED PROMOTION: Wuling Watchguard Captain

Mi Fu was a Qingbo Stockade resident who was later recruited by the Wuling Scientific Developmental District, and was made a watchguard after the completion of Wuling City. Since assuming the role, she has constantly worked at the frontlines, demonstrating extensive knowledge regarding security issues within Wuling City and the peripheral regions, as well as decisiveness and alacrity when handling various emergencies and cases. Mi Fu is committed to Wuling City, has zero tolerance for any form of delinquency or criminality, and always acts with strict justice. She has a good reputation, exercises effective deterrence, and serves as a rallying point for the general public.

Exceptional combat prowess. Impressive physicals and fortitude. Capable of handling high-risk threats. 
Decisive and skilled in executing orders. Capable of making the right calls when facing complex situations. 
Caring and nurturing towards those working under her. Capable of forming a strong, cohesive team. 
Good reputation among the general populace and has earned their trust and support. Public reviews include: "A little blunt but always just." 

AREAS TO IMPROVE ON: 
Over eagerness in applying force. Tendency to employ physical measures when resolving various situations. Lack of procedural awareness. 
Slight disadvantage in clerical work such as report drafting. Limited administrative skills. 
Quick tempered. Lacks patience for communication. Prone to conflicts with others. 
Gives inordinate trust to familiar individuals. Decision-making may be affected by personal relationships and emotions. 

OVERALL RATING: 
Mi Fu has delivered remarkable results in patrol work and law enforcement. Having successfully quelled multiple emergencies, she is a promising officer who can be relied upon for field work. <@profile.key>"Why?"
The legendary senior business consultant of Seš'qa, one of the lead brand managers of the Witching Hour, the downtrodden Sarkaz merchant, "Bridge Builder" Fleming, was taken aback by this simple question. Though it came right out of the blue, Fleming quickly regained his cool, tidied his tie, and started counting the stars as he readied himself for the banter. 
The Feline who stood before him always made him tingle with a strange nervousness, ever since that snowy night. 
"Ahem. First thing first... We genuinely appreciate Endfield's acceptance of Adelheid. Seš'qa hereby extends its most sincere gratitude." 
"Good. That means you'll pay extra for her additional catering fees. Right?" 
"Trust me. Sending her to Endfield is considered a loss for our business." 
"Oh. You have a slogan for Last Rite ... the Princess of the War Court? Very loud and attention grabbing. Must have made you a fortune." 
Fleming laughed. He usually laughs as a means of dealing with his opponent on the negotiating table. But at this moment, he was laughing to give himself a chance to breathe. 
M3 paid no attention to Fleming's peculiarities. Her gaze was reserved for Adelheid, seated uncomfortably outside the office — Last Rite herself. Fleming sensed M3's curiosity. He cannot afford to miss the opportunity to regain his initiative. 
"What do you think of Miss Last Rite?" 
"I think she's hungry," M3 said without averting her gaze from the girl in question. Fleming tried to remember things. Rumors speak of the Feline's ties with the origins of Kazdel, and she hardly paid this much attention to other talents he recommended. "How could you let such a lovely girl starve?" 
"I swear..." 
"I think you need to pay an additional catering fee to Endfield Industries. Maybe we should set this sum to..." 
"I *SWEAR* this is for the best!" 
Fleming immediately realized that he had slipped. His opponent was simply trying to muddy the waters... No. She was just having a friendly banter. Why did he suddenly break his composure? 
"And why is that?" 
"Ugh... You know, a Nachzehrer in a cemetery with an extreme 'shame of consuming'... She has consistently refused to touch the deaths of others. Her constant hunger is only a natural consequence." 
"No, no, no... You got it all wrong..." 
M3 maintained her coy, relaxed tone. But that was not the worst for Fleming. What stressed him out more was the fact that she had not smiled ever since he stepped aboard Dijiang. 
"You know the Sarkaz. No amount of roasted steak fillets could fill an empty soul." 
"Soul? You believe in souls?" 
"Ahem... Every Sarkaz who benefited from the protection of the myriad souls believes in them." 
"I'm sure the myriad souls will be happy to know that," M3 finally moved her gaze away from the girl. She hesitated, a rare opportunity. But Fleming did not treat this as a good sign, "But the time does not match." 
"I understand... It took place over a century ago. Nevertheless, Adelheid is definitely a young girl of only seventeen or eighteen years." 
"Right. So, why?" 
Fleming kept his bitter smile inside. Nevertheless, he decided to confront this question directly. 
"I don't know. But like you said ... she remains very hungry." 
"Even with 'that thing' following her around? That's practically unheard of." 
That genuinely surprised Fleming, if only a little. "Find it rather astonishing that there are things you have not heard about." 
Fleming immediately regretted it when those words blurted out of his mouth. Thankfully, M3 was not in the leisurely mood to interpret his verbal mishap as a taunt. 
"A vast land has perished in her shadow. Millennia-worth of winters heed her beck and call. Yet she remains hungry." 
"It's the blood. We found other Nachzehrers. So many deaths are birthed upon this planet everyday. We have no desire to see another War Court appear without warning. But ... this child is obviously an exception. She has not been 'fed' because she respects every crew mate, messenger, and soldier who died in the frontiers. She could not bring herself to do it. In fact, she refuses to do it." 
"Then how did her power..." 
"'Though she did not consume the dead to strengthen herself, Death remains willing to assist her.' That wendigo friend of yours gave this assessment." 
"...Nezzsalem would be extremely moved if he were here." 
"But that also means the child is destined to take on burdens that shouldn't be hers." 
"I suppose this is the actual reason you recommended her to Endfield." 
"If Adelheid hopes to take upon a path of her choice, I believe Endfield Industries will be her best instructor." 
M3 was obviously taken aback. Fleming himself was also stunned by her reaction. He knew that M3 never expected him to give such a ... soft and compassionate answer. However, he also did not expect M3 to had judged him so poorly. It was a depressing realization for the merchant and consultant. 
"Well, Fleming ... perhaps you are kinder than I thought." 
Those words allowed Fleming's confidence to return. 
"And that is also your kindest evaluation of my character for all these years we've known each other, Miss M3." 
M3 sighed. It would seem she finally allowed herself to relax. "Now, how would you like Endfield to treat her?" 
"The usual," Fleming smiled from the bottom of his heart for the first time in this dialog. "Let her do what she wants, like a normal child. "Age can be a real bummer, old man. Your spearmancy ... got slow and clunky.“ 
The Kuranta thrust the spear into the cracked rooftop and removed the heavy armor pieces. 
"You're just a few years younger than me, so that makes you just as old. Don't tell me that you're still a brat in love with heroic tales." 
"Stop being stupid and head back with me. The warlord Jakub is dead. His dream of 'an even greater city' is no more. This isn't worth dying for." 

"I thought you'd see things my way." the Kuranta looked at the Liberi who stepped over the body of the thirty-ninth Landbreaker, then drew a short blade from a once-ornate scabbard covered in decades of rust. The blade itself glimmered coldly. "I believe in the dream, the one our mentor told us when we were handed these blades. Go back to Terra and let the Golden Age return again. But an Ankhor smashed his tomb. We even couldn't make our way back to the north of Talos-II... Jakub wasn't the only one disappointed. You treat us as dreamers. Tell me then, what is that utopia thing long promised by the Civilization Band when we're facing 'occasional' supply shortages, encroaching Blight masses, and Aggelos attacks?" 

The Liberi sighed with resignation, stopped ten paces away from the Kuranta, pressed a boot into the windswept dust, and made the roof creak. 
"You chose a good place. Strong winds on the roof. The fowlbeasts could easily soar without flapping their wings." 
"Strong winds indeed ... but they're dying down." the Kuranta raised the blade, "We won the Aggeloi War. But what happened next? We're getting old. I'll never live to see my mentor's dream if I kept waiting. I have to act." 
"That's no excuse for following Jakub and pointing our mentor's lance against those who have even less and suffer more." 
"The strong devours the weak. Someone had to do it." the Kuranta straightened and gave a few rather clumsy swings of the blade, "I chose this path to fulfill our mentor's dream... You can't stop me." 
"You were once a hero who charged for ten miles to save a village from an Aggelos attack," the Liberi drew a weapon. It was the exact same sword wielded by the Kuranta. 
He still remembered the day when their mentor handed the blades to them and how his eyes sparkled the moment his fingers touched the weapon. He remembered how his sworn brother asked for their mentor's lance, and how he laughed when his sworn brother boasted about becoming a "great hero". Why did he laugh? The reason escaped his memories. 

"Hero? I'm no hero," the Kuranta raised the blade to chest level, "The hero you mentioned only lives in your mind, or he probably died that night." 
"Your actions disgrace our mentor's lance." the Liberi's handcannon was out of etched ammo and he tossed it away before charging towards the Kuranta, "Return it." 
"See if you're good enough ... to take it off my hands."

<@profile.key>DOCUMENT: Archived operational records (OBSOLETE) 
"Operator Estella, you were instrumental to the success of our espionage and counter-espionage mission against the surviving Landbreaker elements that infiltrated this area. For operational debriefing, we must now go over details of the following achievements we made in the field. They will be used as reference and instructional materials for our future operations." 
"Okay. You flatter me." 
"How did you successfully avoid enemy's feint and correctly deduce actions of the main attacking force?" 
"I ... uh... I was conducting voluntary standby. When I'm done standing by, the enemy's main force were within visual range." 
"In other words, can we assume you have received a relevant order? Sounds like incredible foresight. Did Captain Akekuri give you that order?" 
"I believe it was given to me by electrolytic imbalance and accumulation of anaerobic metabolites. At least that's what I felt..." 
"So... You're trying to say that you missed the enemy's feint attack because you were resting, but woke up to encounter the main enemy force? Okay... Erm... Next question." 
"So, how did you intercept the enemy's operational pass code and decipher their subsequent actions?" 
"The beat wasn't right. I heard it." 
"Beat? What's the beat?" 
"I spent a day in the camp of the surviving Landbreakers. They kept playing the DEATH☆DREAMS album. I have always been a fan since I was little. Akekuri and Fluorite called it noisy so I stopped playing it." 
"Can we get to the point, please...?" 
"Well, DEATH☆DREAMS has a simple structure. The drums were played on 4/4. I knew the rhythm and tempo of every song on the album. But the beats were off that day. Bass was off. There's a sound that's constantly changing lurking under the drums." 
"I'm afraid I'm losing you there. What happened next?" 
"I thought it was some wildlands remix so I focused really hard on the beat and jotted it down. And it happened to be a series of breaker codes. I've learned them before. We later rallied and cleared out the outpost and discovered they were using oscillators to send out their codes. DEATH☆DREAMS was just the camouflage. What a waste of good music." 
"Well... regardless, you successfully provided us with key intel. Thank you. This will be the end of our inquiry."
