1116333865260202771:
She began to think why she was selected for this mission.
It was because of her mastery of the cryogenic Arts and adaptation to the icefields, but more importantly, it was her wildlands pathfinding skills. It was intuitive to her. She could read the stars in the night skies and use them as guiding beacons. The Order of Steel Oath was only founded barely a year ago. She was the best candidate for a scout and someone capable of re-establishing a link between the severed civilizations.
She understood her mission and set off with that hard drive.
The hard drive contained all the data that the Order of Steel Oath collected over the year about the North, their enemies, and their allies. The fearless souls once stepped out of the group and assembled in a separate formation. They recited their steel hard oaths and left Civilization to head into the North, back into the devastated fields of war. There they used themselves as lures to divert Aggeloid offensives... Many people treated their departure as a sign — A sign for the impending disintegration of Civilization. The pessimists believed that once Civilization began mobilizing people to sacrifice themselves, it would inevitably continue to check certain groups people for the grinder... These self-sacrificing individuals, whom we now call the Oathkeepers, were aware of this. Hence, they must re-connect the Civilizations. The information earned with their lives must become a navigational star to light the way ahead.
And now this small, nascent "star" rested in the courier's backpack. She panted heavily with every step through the cold air and snow.
Blood coursed down her arms and dripped all over the ground. Her left arm and left leg were almost completely shattered. She felt every white, hot jolt of pain as bits of bone grated against the soft tissue. Her wounds were inflicted by a new Aggeloid that was never catalogued. The courier thought about the gates of the fort... Perhaps the abomination was created as a siege weapon.
Random thoughts surged through her mind. When the Oathkeepers first marched North, they encountered uncatalogued Aggeloi nearly every day. It would seem that they were beset by an interrogator more than eager to showcase his repertoire of torture devices. Aggeloi designed to kill and massacre with ever-increasing efficacy started to appear throughout the battlefield. Defeating this host will be costly — It will require uncountable lives hellbent on a relentless march...
"Defeating the host... That's right..."
The courier suddenly remembered that she was still alive. She, not the Aggelos, was the victor of that battle... She was the one that froze that long, heavy, and rampaging agglomeration of rock ... and shattered it to pieces... Its fragments glittered in the sunlight like the stars themselves.
Other thoughts began to surface.
"The stars can guide my way. Mom and Dad taught me that they could guide travelers in the wildlands... No... We are the stars themselves... I must tell them that we stood our ground in the far North where it is colder than death... They will hear this ... and ignite the embers of hope..."
More of her blood flowed and seeped into the permafrost.
"But where is the star? Is it in my hands?
"Where am I?
"I cannot see it. The night looms before my eyes, but why ... why won't any of the stars glitter for me?"
......
"It's because the old stars have faded away, but the new stars have yet to be born..."
She tried to raise her hand as high as she could... Her Arts caused the ice to sprout from the bloodsoaked earth beneath her, creep up her body, smother her face, course across the length of her arm, and reach skywards. Its tip was directed towards safety.
"Go higher, and higher still... Be the nova that points the way." Her final thought was crystallized. All that was left was the nascent star wholly forged of frigid ice.
......
She would not know that after many weeks, other couriers followed her guide and reached further south. Their journey ended at the edge of the permafrost. More followed, singers of painful hannas, travelers who need to cross the fields of war...
The little "nova" was handed to many people. In its final destination, the great vessel named Dijiang used it to light the northern skies.

"It looks like a well..."
He rested his elbow upon the railings of the observation deck and allowed his gaze to trail after the twelfth empty bottle sailing through the air before plummeting into the faraway sea. He then saw the majestic "ring", the facility where he works. This was his first time gazing upon it from such a great height.
"What is its purpose? Some kind of an underwater shelter? I think I heard mentioned it's for the firing or launching of something..."
He started making wild guesses but quickly restrained his surging thoughts. The existence of this facility had nothing to do with him... If he had taken the selection trials just a few months ago, before he lost an eye and his entire team in the battlefield, he might have seen the top secret work being carried out inside the place. But now, he no longer felt the pride nor drive of contributing to the future of humanity. Those virtues had been buried beneath his comrades' bones.
He's now just a common deck scrubber... "Who's my employer again?" he thought as he looked down at his work ID. Endfield Industries. Whatever. They're all the same... Endfield, UWST, TGCC, HAS... This place was filled with all sorts of people.
The top brass of every faction gathered at this locale, far removed from the major theaters of war, to work on some mega-projects again...
"It probably end up failing. The frontlines are collapsing one after another. Habitable areas are being squeezed out of existence. Can they really find something to turn the tide of defeat?
"Ugh. Stop thinking about it... I'm just gonna get a headache..."
If he were to live out his days without a care, he should take it to the extremes. But he still heard them talk behind his back — The only child of a proud family of soldiers. The rising young star who gave in to self-loathing, who willingly took up a deck scrubber's job so he could be as far away as he could from the battlefields — Oh yes, his ears still caught wind of that every now and then.
He was surprised how these words could still hurt him. That was why he came to this place to release himself. Of course, that release inevitably evolved into self-pity and many bottles of kohl.
The thirteenth empty bottle flew and fell into the sea.
So why did he feel so terrible? Was there something that he could not put to rest? Medals? He threw them away. His preferred weapon? He couldn't even remember where he buried it. "Oh... Yes, there is indeed something else."
He took off his eye patch, then scooped out the thing that never warmed from his socket. The prosthetic eye of gold and Origocrust stared at him from his palm. In the story passed down through the generations, the eye was fashioned out of gold rewarded by the emperors... His ancestors strode the fields in the Battle of the Four Emperors and witnessed the fall of Gaul... It did not matter if they became powerful magnates or explorers of Terra. The eye was always handed down to the next in line. He, the disgraced failure, was the last inheritor.
The glory of his house shone through the pupil hemmed by golden filigree, and it cast a spine-chilling glare into his soul.
He clenched his fist and closed his fingers around the heirloom of an unbroken line, then cast it into the sea without hesitation.
"There. It is done. All clean and quiet."
The kohl within him swirled and made him burp. That ring in the far distance looked more and more like a well. He remembered the wishing well he saw in a small village he chanced upon during his Grand Tour of Terra. People threw coins of gold and silver into the well and prayed for their wishes to come true. The price of the item cast into the well would determine the scope of the wish manifested.
"Hurhur. Bunch of fools."
If that were true, what about the thing he just threw into that well? What wish could it hope to accomplish?
The eye was a prized treasure that witnessed the fall of great nations, transforming civilizations, carnage, rebirth, destruction, and perseverance. Would the well mold it into something else?
"Forget it. I'd rather sleep this off."
He raised his hand and launched the fourteenth bottle into the air, and followed its trail until it was held in stasis in mid-air.
The wishing well had granted its response.

A complete silence was followed by the emergence of an enormous crystal formation.
The heavens were rent asunder and revealed a path of Originium.
Countless figures of grand majesty stood amongst the clouds by the end of this long road. A massive Cosmic Gate appeared behind them.
"Why, Your Majesties? Why?
"Is it because I have cast away your gift? Because I abandoned my history, my lineage, and all my glories?"
His fallen comrades sprouted from the Originium road. They stretched out their withered limbs and shattered weapons, and did all they could to make him stay.
So he took out a spear.
Every carcass he pierced revealed a great many words. He bowed his head to read these weighty words and revealed them to be names.
He saw the names of his father, his grandfather, the pasha, the pope, the inquisitor, the frontiersmate, the miner...
He followed the River of the Dead and walked past the historical figures.
Finally, the emperors left their names upon the tip of spear.
With that, he raised the broken spear up high, and made a great thrust against the massive gate before the deafening roars woke him.
The great ring in the distance opened up the sea. That piercing spear, the monumental construct forged by every faction with every moment of despair, every sliver of hope, and every weeping wound, was thrust into the heavens above.

And on ██/██, ██, was Dijiang successfully launched.

<@profile.key>The Oathkeepers have twenty words for rain. When I saw her again, it felt as though she had been smothered and battered by each and every type of the downpours. 
"Azrila," I said, "We all make mistakes." 
Those were feeble words. I had never served in any assault banner, and I was not at the frontlines. Like the others, I still had zero knowledge how she survived the living hell. I had no intention of paying any heed to the festering rumors — doubting your fellow Oathkeeper was a path to calamity. Even if the concerns were grounded in reasonable doubt, any fracture should never emerge from within. 
She remained silent and swept the surroundings with her stiff gaze. No one else came to see her off. This was the first time when I failed to read her expressions. It was not sadness, but neither was it release. I thought I could hear her breathe a sigh of relief. 
"The Castellan has given his verdict." I said. 
I wanted to give her a pat on the shoulder but quickly realized it wasn't the right thing to do. For the first time, her pauldrons seemed too big for her, and the straps rattled against her dagger. 
There was no way we could fit the cremation urns of twenty-eight Oathkeepers into her baggage, no matter how hard we tried. Azrila settled on something else, insisting on carrying their service tags with her at all times. They clattered and rang with every movement, but no one laughed. 
"Nilla's weapon has been placed in the Vault of Relics. Her family will be here in a few days to retrieve her other things. Don't you want to go and see them again?" 
"No," she finally spoke, "I intend to set off at once." 
Nilla's family placed great importance on traditions, and turned down the Order's request of returning the cremation urns and her personal effects. 
Perhaps I should not question any further. My neck slightly itched. Perhaps several pairs of eyes were gazing at this place from behind the safety of the windows and blinds that demarcated the boundaries. 
"Go forth and see to our mission." I opened the gates of the keep. The vehicle was already loaded and had been waiting for a while. The driver was meticulously cleaning the mud from the bumpers as it always rained in the north. "I shall look after your patron firearm. I swear it by my name."  
"Gratitude, Grand Treasurer." Azrila then paused for a while. 
"The Crusade will eventually end." </>

...Let me get this straight. Your team lost to Z7 in the combat drill 'cause you didn't graduate from a military school and Lil' Dodge wasn't your instructor?
Enough excuses, kid. I trained tons of raw recruits like you and I totally lost count on the number of losers who hamstring themselves by boo-hooing about their sad backstories.
Look at your face! Do you think I'm gonna give you a motivational story how a missing degree or diploma isn't that important? HAH! WRONG! I'm your friggin' instructor, not your pathetic shrink! I'm not going to make you feel good about your academic failures!
Since we mentioned degrees, then I gotta say — it's actually pretty important.
But if you're missing one, there are solutions to go about it.

I became an instructor after all. Guess how I did it?
WRONG AGAIN! I, Sato Kogo, never read a proper book in my life. In fact, I only learned how to write in Victorian thanks to courses offered aboard Dijiang. When I was your age, I was just a bummed out debt collector in Neo Tsukushi!
Wha? Don't you know what a debt collector is...? Ugh. Forget it. I'll put it simply. Hired muscle. That was my job.
So did that for about three or four years. I was either bruising people or getting bruised myself. As long as someone paid the creds, it didn't really matter to me.

I was in my twenties and I thought I'd be doing that for the rest of my life... I never expected something big to happen.
Oh yes... Stepped on a few toes. The wrong tail, actually. Not some cartel security firm, but an actual big shot oyabun.
Ugh. This is exactly why I kept telling you to pay attention to the surroundings when you fight. I learned it the very hard way, so at least take this from me.

Weather was great that day. I besieged that gambling den with two dozen bros from the organization. There were just around eight people on the other side and I thought it would be a cakewalk.
But those dudes fought like beasts in heat. Half of the lads were down in a heartbeat. I was out of ideas but I couldn't just leave my bros behind. So I came up with the clever idea of using the revolving doors...
How did I do it? Well, i simply undid the security latch and got it spinning... Anyways, I got two enemies down in an instant. Some of the bros started helping and we sent the rest of them packing.
There was one thing I miscalculated. The revolving door was connected to the one upstairs. Now that wouldn't sound like a thing but my boss suddenly got the bright idea of enjoying the spectacle. Suffice to say, his tail got caught — Boss man was also a Lupo and you know what they do when somebody messes with their tail.
What happened next? Geesh. Do I have to spell it out? I escaped to the frontiers before they gave me cement shoes! I slogged two years in trucking, four in janitorial work, and three in bounty hunting. My liver was dying on me and luck finally turned when I arrived at Endfield — Some old client wrote me a recommendation. Thank the Big Gas for that.

Alright. Your turn. Tell me about your plans on beating Z7 next time?

<@profile.key>While serving as a messenger in our Specialist Tech Division, Operator Avywenna could not give a more different vibe than Operator Gilberta. The latter is known throughout Endfield for her uninhibited sweetness and geniality. Avywenna, on the other hand, approaches socializing like a professional and manages relationships accordingly. 
One has to work with Operator Avywenna for extended periods of time before noticing her peculiar quirks. For example, despite being extremely loquacious during small gatherings or in private, everyone who recalled the exchanges would realize that they hardly got any truth from Avywenna — especially about herself. Nevertheless, people tend to find themselves spilling their beans with Avywenna as she proved to be an excellent listener. She is always capable of asking friendly questions, leading on discussions along the direction she has planned, and concluding dialogs at just the perfect moments. 
Avywenna personally explained such skills with her background. She was born to a huge Cautus family living in the Free City of Alloycarrot. Patience easily becomes the most important virtue when living with a huge number of kin. This claim has been verified. Querying "Avywenna" in the population database of Alloycarrot gives you over 80 individuals with the same name. 
Whenever Avywenna casually drops a morsel of info about herself, it's always a subtle bait to get her conversational partner to lay everything out. A short dialog is all she needs to acquire background information and contacts about everyone she is chatting with. Avywenna would also argue, with great cunning, that she did so out of professional habit that carried over from her messenger career, where one must constantly deal with people. 
One thing to note: no one resents Avywenna's air of mystery. Instead, it only got more people interested in chatting her up. Her presence has greatly enhanced Endfield's ability to navigate the local affairs that are often tangled and delicate. Avywenna is a master at resolving conflicts and diffusing tension, walking away without a scratch. She is like a miner navigating the criss-crossing mines and tunnels of Alloycarrot. The one directing the situation will never feel lost.</>

<@profile.key>[Graduation Speech] 
"Hmmm... Greetings, everyone. I am Zhuang Fangyi from the Class of ██. It is truly an honor to stand here today on behalf of my fellow graduates. 
"I'm the youngest amongst you. Even fellow students who just enrolled are two years ahead of me. So I'd like to begin by thanking everyone for your care and support throughout these years. 
"Thank you for helping me reach the top shelves when I couldn't. Thank you for always saving me a front-row seat for the lectures. Thank you for holding back your frustration even when experiments stalled... 
"Most of all, although everyone spoiled me with loving exceptions usually reserved to a younger sibling, none of my ideas or suggestions were ever brushed off as childish. I skipped many years in school and lost the chance to befriend peers of my age. But in return, I gained invaluable friendships with those older than me. I missed out on one kind of companionship, but received guidance, mentorship, and trust from another. 
"Now, my next step is to continue my studies at the Hongshan Academy of Sciences. The colleagues I meet there are likely to be even more experienced... I also hope to learn from them and build new friendships..." 

[Eulogy] 
"I am keenly aware that many among you are far more suited than I to stand here today and deliver this eulogy for those we have lost. In the presence of parents, sons and daughters, lifelong companions, and loved ones ... I am but a mere youth. 
"I was the youngest member at the Science Station. The reason I could convey our longing on behalf of everyone is a result of your patience, guidance, and care... 
"I have made a journey blessed with support from all sides. I often asked my experienced peers how I might repay the trust and sincerity they showed me. They would always smile and tell me that doing my work and honoring the expectations placed upon me were the best means of repayment. 
"Though they are no longer with us, the trust they invested in me has not waned, nor has their faith in the Xiranite project. I understand that this is the moment to repay them in full... 
"And faithfully I shall bear those hopes and expectations upon my shoulders." 

Orientation Speech 
"Greetings, everyone. It is a great honor to welcome you to Wuling, where you have chosen to commit your most beautiful years to the laboratories, to this place, and to the forefront of our fight against the Blight and the Rift. 
"I know many of you chose Wuling because your parents and elders who sacrificed everything for the Science Station... Seeing your young, eager faces brings back memories — I sat where you are seated right now, and listened to your parents and elders who led me onto this path. 
"I once thought their greatest gift to me was the scientific achievements they had spent their lives creating. Now I realize the gift includes you who arrived at Wuling — who answered their call to follow their footsteps. 
"I once believed that the best way to honor their memories was to stay on that path and reach, without hesitation, the ideal future they dreamed of. Now I understand that I must also lead those who follow, to guide them onto that path and help them envision the future... 
"Thank you. 
"Thank you for choosing to walk this path with me." 

Recording: New Operator Welcome Party 
"Am I tipsy already? Maybe a bit... But this isn't right. I only had a little.. 
"Is this the ninth? Hmm ... maybe it's a bit too much. 
"You know, the last time I felt this happy was when I first arrived at the Science Station. They threw me a welcome party too. 
"I was very young back then so I only had juice. But I felt tipsy just the same, watching them toast cup after cup and laugh without worry. The mood was perfect. 
"Today ... feels just like that again. The future is laid out before me, waiting for me to step forward. 
"What more is there to say? Nothing... Just being happy is enough."</>

5781618409543038911:
I once had extreme confidence.
Confidence for my gifts in wielding the (applicable) Originium Arts. And my gifts were rare indeed, even when taking every caster of Talos-II into account.
I believe all of my Arts instructors I had since my childhood could attest to this fact, and there were 23 of them.
While my peers struggled to light a candle with an Arts Unit, I was debating the possibility of having an unaided Infected cast the Arts for extended periods time and at higher throughputs... It was a time when I first heard about the legendary Endministrator. Back then, at least, I once believed that I might be capable of achieving the same.
My performances in the Originium Arts Proficiency Assessment for the last 20 years, my GPA from the courses on Originium Arts theories during the academy, and the accolades I received for my graduation thesis titled The Gap Between Practical Applications and Theory — A Discourse on the Future of the Originium Arts, only served to strengthen my belief as I spent every year perfecting my Arts. There is a significant possibility that I am a "genius".
— And I held on to that belief until I joined the company that I have dreamed about since my childhood. Endfield Industries.

I could hardly describe my feelings when I underwent the routine integrated physical examinations for new employees and received the report.
— My Originium Arts Assimilation was rated as "Standard". How was it possible? They must have made a mistake.
At that moment, I felt as though I was struck by the devious Arts of a Djall, and it struck so hard I could fight off the mental fog.
When I came to my senses, I went straight to the Human Resources Division and delivered a severe protest. I demanded a re-examination and declared my absolute refusal to accept such a brusque conclusion made without sufficient evidence.
The HR Division seemed to be expecting my applications. I was entreated by Martin Marvin Malen in a most sincere manner.
"...We understand your requests and have arranged two additional Originium Arts Assimilation testing sessions after three working days. A total of two operators will also be assigned to take the tests with you and serve as control references."

Three days later —
As per the instructions, I cut out a perfect square out of a ferric slab before me with my Arts Unit. I turned around saw the Savra who should be at the opposing testing station. He looked at me curiously.
"Is this the way to do it? I thought I had to cut 16 squares with a single move!"
This is my confession. I thought I heard him wrongly and subconsciously gazed at the results of his test... And I saw sixteen perfect squares neatly laid out on the floor of the training cabin. The clock stopped at exactly 1 minute and 1 second.
— What was I doing at that time? Oh, I just finished calibrating my Arts Unit and thought about the perfect approach to start cutting the slab.

There was no question that I lost the first trial. It was a complete disaster.
But negativity had yet to catch up to me. I simply prepped for the second session. I comforted myself with this thought: "Endfield's a big place, and they have a legend like the Endministrator. A fellow Endfielder of such competence ... should be something to expect."
Soon, an accident, or the stroke of Fate ... dawned upon me.
While I was checking the Arts Unit, an Ægir youth wearing an elite operator's uniform poked his head out of the training cabin. He simply wagged his tail and undid the safeties of over fifty standard Arts Units. They orbited him like an obedient school of fins as he left the place and mumbled these words: "What a hassle... Shouldn't have come here at the first place..."
This was when I first experienced despair from seeing an "unattainable gap" that could never be closed.
I learned that even if I mastered every form of Originium Arts to my knowledge, the tracelessness and effortless elegance of his Arts wielding were qualities that I could never achieve...
Never, not in my entire lifetime.
I suddenly felt that all my achievements in the Arts for the last twenty years only gave me better knowledge of what I witnessed at a particular moment in life — I am not the prodigy. That title belongs to someone else.
I chose to forfeit the second testing session.

After the test, I also gave up joining the Specialist Tech Division. Thankfully, the Arsenal took a good look at my CV and asked if I was interested in doing some weapon engineering.
I agreed.

They said that the classic "Arts Identifier" would be returning for the Arts Unit Obstacle Challenge this year — I received five of those, but I would not mind getting a sixth.

2145752065466328381:
My ancestor was a well-learned man who lived at Shangshu. During one of his journeys, he encountered a sudden downpour that forced him to seek shelter beneath the cliffs. He made a warming fire with dried grass, and was about to sleep when he saw a strange individual wearing jet-black clothing. The entity had no eyes nor mouth and its arm was joined to the mountain itself. My ancestor thus asked this strange entity: "Sir, why is your arm joined with the rock?" 
The strange being replied: 
"I once lived in Baizao. One day, I dreamed of a tiny figure dressed in yellow who stood in the middle of my palm and it asked me about the weight of human life. 'It is heavier than the mountains.' I answered.
"The tiny figure smiled and replied: 'And I am the Ruler of the Kingdom in the Palm.' And with that, the tiny figure disappeared and was never seen again. I did not want to overturn its kingdom, and thus I placed my hand upon this very place and did not move it for a century. As the years passed, a great mountain gradually rose from my palm. You are looking at it right now."
My ancestor was confused and asked: "You are a kind and caring soul, but why allow yourself to be trapped here for so long? Your concerns are genuine and true, but why don't you severe your hand and be freed from this place?"
The strange being mused: "I do not know which weighs more — the Kingdom Upon the Palm, or the Palm Before My Wrist. Perhaps if I found the answer, I would be able to bear the weight of this mountain and travel with it."
The strange being then continued: "Now, leave me in peace, and you shall have yours." With that, my ancestor fell asleep. Dawn broke, but the strange being was not seen again. 

I also heard about a herb that goes by the name Zhenhuang. The grass is mildly toxic and burning it generates hallucinogenic fumes. Perhaps this ancestor of mine had breathed in a whiff too many!

<@profile.key>DOCUMENT: List of Candidates for the Vanguard Scientist Award 
Author: Luo Shiqiao 

After integrating observations for the three dimensions of innovation, influence, and adaptability, I recommend Tianshi Pan Yuan as the recipient for this year's Vanguard Scientist award. His work so far accrued a total of twelve academic achievements and he has attained six sustainable development goals for HAS. Very few awardees from the last ten years have achievements on par with his. And Da Pan is not yet thirty. 
Although I am his mentor, I can guarantee that my evaluations are completely fair and balanced. When Pan Yuan knocked on my door and described his wish to be on my project team, my first reaction was to turn him down. The young man had left a relatively poor impression with me back then. He played ping-pong with explosives, on fire. He also got several veteran (and well respected) Tianshi to perform tap dance on a digital poster of Creative Maolaguo Cuisine Lovers. He built several high-speed battleships from scraps, and attacked our subterranean cryostorage facility with his fleet. The entire building reeked of rotten fins for a month... Yes. I suppose these are minor misdemeanors that come naturally to the youths. HAS encourages all kinds of scientific exploration, and even I ended up in the emergency medical bay a few times back in my younger days. 
Certain youths play pranks to get attention. Some of them do so to sate their immense curiosity about the world. Pan Yuan doesn't quite belong to either of these categories. He is ... too smart. I saw disinterested boredom in his eyes when he was caught doing these pranks. After becoming his mentor, I realized that he committed these actions because he could. To put it in other words, he wanted to prove that he was simply better than anyone else in HAS — even when it came to pulling off pranks on campus. 
Joy comes from challenges. Take away the challenge and you deprive any opportunities for joy — and a joyless academic pursuit will never get far. A sculptor who spends every moment chipping away at stone would only leave a handful of works behind. Pan Yuan has proved to be most obstinate. This stone must be properly polished to reveal its true beauty. But only another slab of stone harder than him could hope to bring down his pride and chip away at his edges. 
I told him, "There are several Tianshi who made significant achievements in the field of rift research. They would be better mentors than me..." 
But Pan Yuan replied, "But there is a great mountain within me that must be conquered first. Your projects and research focus are the only things that match my goals." 
At that moment, I saw confusion, pain, and maybe a subtle dash of cautious hope in his eyes. Maybe my judgment on his character was not entirely correct. Perhaps something changed him. As long as he is persistent, I have faith he will change for the better. 

And if you must have a reason for not giving him the award ... there is the matter of his rather impulsive temperament. And also because he was cooking in the lab and deliberately mislabeled a tub of puffed rice as "Reducing Agent". Maybe he didn't want others to steal his food, but this action completely wrecked my first prototype! </>

APPLICANT: Akekuri 
ROLE: Rotational Operator, Specialist Tech Division 
Dear Supervisor Perlica, 
I have learned that the Operational Axis is currently recruiting a new leader for Operations Team Z7 within Endfield Industries. Therefore, I am writing to formally apply for the position. 
To my knowledge, Operations Team Z7 was originally a multipurpose support unit. Its former members have since been promoted or reassigned to other teams, leaving the unit inactive. Given the growing multi-front operational demands faced by Endfield Industries, as well as the ongoing personnel shortages within the Specialist Tech Division, I intend to rebuild Z7 as a compact, agile support team capable of independently handling low- to mid-risk missions while assisting other task forces when needed — all without drawing heavily on existing resources. 
I have completed all required field training, earning A or higher ratings in 32 real missions and over 200 simulations, and I have solid experience in on-site coordination and leadership. 
If required, I can also take on administrative duties and serve as a point of contact between Management Axis and Operational Axis. 
If approved, I will begin recruitment and training immediately to get the team mission-ready in the shortest time possible. 
A summary and detailed proposal are attached for your consideration. 
Sincerely, 
Akekuri

DOCUMENT: Excerpt from a diary 
Four years have passed since I boarded this vessel. The task of repair is progressing slowly, but with efficacy. Although the undertaking has become relatively uneventful, I have gradually found my way to return to my inner calm. This is the place where I can work in a dark and cold cabin. The rhythms of machines offer me incredible comfort. This is where I need not worry whether my actions would bring trouble to the others. Of course, this is also where I can share fragmented conversations with data residues of the Originium Network. In the Network, I experienced never-seen-before ruins of splendorous majesty that Sankta share their empathy. I heard the lamentations from myriad souls of the Sarkaz erased from existence. I witnessed the incessant bleeding of rebellion and subservience. And every time I wanted to take another step, these experiences would suddenly cease. The silence is frightening. I continued my calculations and repairs, hoping I can hear it speak once more. 
............ 
Something I feared even more has happened. I realized that the Originium has been polluted, damaged, and obliterated. It seems intertwined with what I perused in the various tomes of the Cabal. But why is this the case? What does Originium mean with regards to the codes of civilization that we are deciphering? And what is the entity capable of polluting, damaging, and even obliterating the Originium? 
Perhaps this is why Abbess Mumu sent me here. 
............ 
That was the day when I noticed a strange glow on Supervisor Perlica's visage. But this glow was quickly extinguished by her constant pondering. They are whispering. Something big is about to happen. Will it be relevant to the answers I seek? 
............ 
Black hair, black mask, and black shadow. Operator Chen Qianyu introduced the Endministrator to me. The one who had been hibernating in the medical bay. 
And for an instant, I seemed to achieve a form of empathy. A cacophony and impulse for joy, laughter, and tears exploded within me. I could not restrain the shaking of my material form. This entity is the answer, but I have not prepared my questions. </>

<@profile.key>What do I think of the north? Worst place ever ... I swear! I seriously messed up agreeing to join Rooter on his hunt for that mysterious Sami vendor out in the middle of nowhere! We went over the first snowpeak and were barely two days into the north when some Blighted snowstorm "caught" us at the foot of the mountains! 
I will never forget the sight of an entire burdenbeast being swooshed away by the Blight-tainted snow. The only thing on my mind was: "Blasted blightery! I'm gonna die here..." 
But I guess I saved up enough luck for the past decade or so! The snowstorm was just meters away from us when an Ursus girl swooped in from the skies — I kid you not! She flew in on a snowboard, pulled off a perfect landing next to us, slammed a shield on the ground, and suddenly a wall of ice appeared with a WOOSH! That wall kept the snowstorm away! 
Anyway, she saved both Rooter and me. She escorted us into a cave that she called our temporary shelter. 
And there were all sorts of people there... Oathkeepers, Seš'qa caravan drivers, and even Landbreakers! 
I still remember how we just walked in and some tall and mean-looking Feline started pointing his finger at us, "These two! They're frauds plotting to bring their swindling ways to Sami! I heard all about their dirty plots along the way. Why are you saving these lowlives? Don't let them cheat you!" It was only then when I suddenly recognized the Feline. He was the guide who traveled with us a few days back... I had wondered why he suddenly returned the commission and refused to guide us any longer... 
Anyway, I thought we were finished but the Ursus lass who brought us in said nothing. She gave the Feline a glance and the big mean kittyboy ... just sat down and said nothing else. 
I wanted to thank her personally back then, but she soon rushed out to carry on with her SAR. I couldn't even get her name. Another SAR team soon arrived and brought us to safety. 
But I recognized the badges and markings on her outfit. They were the same as the illustrations in the shelter. 
What happened next...? Well, I found your place. That's what happened. Hah! Just take these supplies. My token of gratitude to that Ursus lass! 
— Recordings from a donor of the Northern Corridor Rescue Union </>

Messenger? Never head that name before.

Wars?

Anyways, I din't want to lend her my burdenbeast.

She sed we lost our link with Terra but Messengers like her wud try to bring everyone on Talos-II together and biuld trust instead of walls.

She gave me this jentoe smile plus a floating metal ball flowting close to her. She sed its mighty expensiff, worth almost as much as her letter. Tolds me I can keep the flowting ball as a dee-paw-zit until she comes back with my burdenbeast.
Yeah, flowting stoff is usually expensiff.
So I agreed and lent her my burdenbeast. I tolds her my name and showed her the way to the villejj.
......

She said the Age of Messengers is coming! I think she was happy when she wrotes that.
The package contains this "comms radio" with some instructions. Now everyone in the villejj can use this "radio" and call other Messengers nearby.
But who shud I wryt to? And where should I send my letter? I never left my villejj.
Maybe I should wryt to that Lady Messenger.

<@profile.key>According to her birth certificate (which she found after an extended search through her personal belongings), "Chen" was born at a place far outside the Civilization Band in the Year 132. She does not recognize the name of the place or what happened there. Thankfully, she remembers everything about her wonderful childhood at Hongshan City. 
For example, the first sight of her memories was an evening where she was lying in her mother's embrace. The sharp ridges of Hongshan Crater resembled spears behind a wall of shields, like ancient fists raised high into the night skies of Talos-II. 
The first word she spoke in her memories was "Mom!" that she voiced into an echo tube with plenty of jiggles. The echoes made it sound like a chorus of a thousand voices. And Chen remembered her mother saying, "Jianshan, we should call her Qianyu. She'll probably end up at the bottom of her class like I did, so a simpler name will make it easier when the teacher makes her write it over and over." 
The first sword of her memories was a stick carefully trimmed and sanded to remove all the thorns, barbs, and bark. 
The first reward of her memories was a gentle kiss on her head, awarded after she disarmed the wielder of another stick. 
The first time she understood things in her memories was when the grown-ups announced the Aggeloi had arrived. Her mother suddenly opened a door hidden within the wardrobe and took out a blade she never seen before, and rushed out of their home. 
The first sad moment in her memories was after her tenth birthday party. Her father called her and she went over. He wiped the cream off her cheeks, told her the news, and she never saw her mother ever since. 

"I thought it was no big deal." Chen Qianyu said. She had just met a Liberi this afternoon — One that called herself Perlica. Though she resembled a TGCC heiress, she claimed she came from a place called Endfield. The two shared a Mo bun besides a mud trail. Although Chen was the one who put in a great deal more effort to push that burdenbeast cart, the quiet and well-behaved Perlica ate way more than she did. Then again, Chen got a smaller share because she spent most of that afternoon sharing moments from the first twenty years of her life. 
"So it means —" Perlica said, "that was the day when she suddenly disappeared from your life." 
"She didn't disappear," Chen Qianyu said, "I know she's still alive. We just don't know where she went and when she'd be back. She also made a very important promise with me!" 
Perlica nodded. 
"Okay, I've shared more than enough already! What about your family, Perlica? Tell me about them!" 
"Just like yours," Perlica said quietly, "I don't know ... when my family would return. And we also made an important promise..." 
"Oh, I guess we're really fated to meet each other!" 
Chen grabbed the Liberi's shoulder and felt her stiffen up temporarily before relaxing. </>

<@profile.key>Endministrator and Supervisor Perlica of Endfield Industries: 
I am extremely pleased to learn that Laevatain has returned with the Endministrator's help. Though her journey is far from complete, her return proves that she has found a new objective and people whom she is willing to travel with. 
Extremely powerful "desire and hope" drove Laevatain to step onto the lands of Talos-II. When we first sensed her existence, the light she gave off was bedazzling. I later realized that this light was emitted by her obsession — her innermost ego demanding the answer: "Who am I?" 
Led on by the said obsession, the fragments awakened and created a complete persona. "She" walked out of the Originium Woods, new and intact, and arrived at Rhodes Island bearing the name "Laevatain". I thought she would immediately become one of our strongest assets and supporters, but she turned us down. Just like Surtr who had always walked alone, no one can command Laevatain or force her to stay in one place. She will answer to no faction until she finds the answer to dispel her own miasma of amnesia. Hence, we decided to open the doors and give her our best farewells. 
Once, I was worried that Laevatain's choice would affect other reconveners. Then I realized that they became reconveners because every one of them did not forget the old dream and vision. And that is why they reconvened with you on this very same path. Now, this thought alone has lifted a stone off my chest. 
Since Laevatain is currently an official Endfielder fighting along your side, then allow me to share a few words of advice (based on my knowledge of "her") for "getting along with her". 
Firstly, accommodate and accept Laevatain's straightforward nature. She often says whatever that comes to her mind. It is not an act of hostility, malice, or rudeness. In fact, such words are a symbol of her sincere and undisguised attitude — "I prefer to simply tell you what I'm thinking right now." 
Secondly, should Laevatain exhibit obvious signs of fury or impatience, do not attempt to persuade her to "calm" down. Believe me, there are more effective means, such as the provision of ice cream or other things that can rapidly "cool" the situation. Laevatain is someone you can communicate with, but she dislikes "being told what to do". 
Just as a side note, before she left Rhodes Island, she took all the crimsonberry ice cream from my lab freezer — and ate them all, right before my eyes, as though it was the right thing to do. "Thought you told me memories can lie," she said as she licked the spoon, "So I better have more of this to make it as memorable as possible." Laevatain marked her farewell with this action to ensure the veracity of the moment. She actually cares very deeply about her friends, far more deeply than most would like to think. 
Thirdly, Laevatain is extremely similar to Surtr, but according to her temperament... Do not tell her that she resembles Surtr. Also, do not tell her that she DOES NOT resemble Surtr. In fact, do not ever compare her to Surtr, unless she brings the topic up herself. Always remember this! 
Best wishes in your collective journey across Talos-II. 

Rhodes Island </>

<@profile.key>[Clinical Diagnosis Report]
Imaging scans indicate blurred organ contours with observable abnormal shadows within the operator's body. Detection of Originium particles within the circulatory system shows anomalies, presenting signs of Oripathy. At this stage, the operator can be confirmed as an Oripathy-positive.

Attending Physician's Note: According to Tangtang's own account, she contracted Oripathy during a conflict between Qingbo Stockade and the Tianshi of Wuling City a decade ago. Tangtang stated she received no specialized treatment over these ten years, only various folk remedies provided sporadically by the stockade residents. However, examination results indicate that both her Cell-Originium Assimilation rate and Blood Originium-Crystal Density are remarkably well-controlled.
When questioned about this, Tangtang replied, "Everyone says I'm the River's Daughter. The water washes the sickness away."
Could natural bodies of water truly cure Oripathy? The answer is evident: it's impossible.

[Medication Application Form from a Tianshi]
Generic Medication Name: Oripathy Suppressant
Quantity Requested: Long-term supply
Infection Site of Patient: Ocular region
Reason for Application: Aiding Qingbo Stockade
Audio Log:
"Honestly, I'm a little hesitant about delivering the medication... The first time, he threw it right back at us, shouting, 'We won't take handouts from Wuling people!' and tried to charge at us with his head... Thankfully, the watchguards were there and helped us escape. I'm not afraid he'd kill me, it's just that we can't have another incident like that.
"The girl's Oripathy is on the verge of worsening. We're aware of it, and surely they are too. She contracted it because of us. We have an obligation to treat her.
"Back then ... it was sheer chaos. The sky was pitch black, low, and heavy with rain tearing through the curtain of clouds. We trudged through the howling wind as the stockade residents charged out from behind the hills, weapons in hand, their shadows in the night like malevolent spirits...
"People were terrified. No one noticed there was such a young child in the crowd...
"The rain washed away the blood... No, no, perhaps it never truly vanished. Whenever I close my eyes, I see that girl's wounded eye, and his ... the leader's eyes. The ones that said he just wanted to survive... I will never forget them for as long as I live.
"The second time, we left the syringes near the outskirts of Qingbo Stockade, where the residents were sure to pass by.
"This time, it wasn't charity from an enemy ... maybe it fell from the sky, grew from the earth, or was carried by a beast. Thinking of it that way might make it a little easier for them to accept.
"I waited two whole days ... and it was taken.
"I waited two more days and saw the girl playing by the water. She chased long-ears along the river for quite a distance. She seemed much better.
"I don't know what will happen from here on out ... and I don't think this counts as true atonement. But I had a full night's rest, at least for that day."</>

4074433390663850132:
There was a time when I was confused about life. The underground arenas of the Asphalt Roundabout is usually the first consideration of people of my size and stature. But the desolation of the place shocked me. That was not the place where I'd want to spend the rest of my life in. So I went to La Fantoma, a city of opportunities and a gathering place for the rich and famous! There are cartel joint sessions, forums, and expos! EVERYTHING!
......
One year passed and I splurged all my savings on a vehicle. Some charitable merchant helped me convert it into a nomadic resto, which happens to be the one right here. And I call it a "boat" since it's next to the sea. My "pier" is where I moor my "boat". I even found a few assistants back then. Made a ton of serious creds during the Obsidian Festival when the entire place was packed with tourists.
......
But two years later, I found more and more people doing my thing. They drive up to the place with their truck and started serving the tourists. The Obsidian Festival made and unmade my fortunes... They built more and more fancy hotels but I am getting less and less diners? During that year, I saw a Feline who was just like me. Splurged his entire fortune and ended up with nothing...
......
Three years had passed. I didn't know how long I'd stay afloat. Revenue was dwindling and that Perro made it worse! The stinkin' mutt always parked his food truck opposite mine, and he had the galls to come over to my place and tell my diners that I was almost finished... I felt like killing that bloody runt.
......
I was the last one on the "boat". I started packing my stuff and planned to drive my "boat" back home. But that was the same year when La Fantoma got hit by a tidal wave. When the disaster ended, an Endfield medical SAR team arrived... How has this got anything to do with my store? It's got nothing with my store, but I strode out one night and heard the Endfielders admiring the star-like beauty of this place. I looked around and saw the dark beach cluttered with seashells brought ashore by the great waves. Some of them gave off soft, gentle glows. I suddenly remembered how we used to see all this when they just got the fest going and the crowd was still small. I suddenly had an idea, mortgaged my "boat" on the following day, got myself some glowing shells, and decorated them with various accessories. That's right. You're holding the very same thing. What happened next? Well, we got even more "piers" and my "boat" is coasting along real easy. 
I'll let you in on something. I'm planning to take a contract over this beach. Yes, that's right. The one beneath your feet. I'm going to grind these shells down to create the Evenglow Coast! I even figured out the name — Dreams of the Stardust Sea. Maybe the organizers of Obsidian Festival will choose my beach for their next evening event. Make sure you visit, 'cos I'll get you a fat discount.
What happened to that stinkin' mutt of a Perro? Oh, he's right over there. We're partners now. Why did I choose him? 'Cos business people of La Fantoma are all about helping each other out. That's how we made this place.

Though this wasn't the first time they talked about Bander Scavs, I never really saw one myself.
People can't really appreciate how difficult life could be out there on Talos-II. Band cities and neighborhoods must work closely together to survive, yet many Banders chose to leave the city behind to live as a nomad or prospector in the frontiers.
I myself wasn't too surprised by this. These people had lost too much. I interviewed around a dozen refugees last week from a disaster-stricken neighborhood that ran out of food. They had no other choice.
However, there were also some who refused to live in a world of law or were simply sociopaths. These individuals preferred a life filled with constant violence and danger.
Regardless of their intents, no Bander nomads could truly give up the touch of civilization. Also last week, I saw them craft weapons with a scavenged machine tool. I was extremely curious how they managed to get their hands on a working lathe. The answer was simple. They got lucky with a scavenging run through a Bander city dumpsite. These landfills provided for their every need.
Turned out that Bander Scav was a pretty accurate name for these people.
If you're reading this, tell that little Bander journalist to stop stalking me. People who complain about sleeping bags do not belong in the wildlands. She should get back to her cushy Bander place and stick to being a celebrity tabloid writer.

<@intru.bold>- Protocol Pass -</>
Every item on the Protocol Pass is gathered from official operator interviews conducted by the Arsenal Engineers. These items include support projects that everyone hopes to see.
Activating each seasonal Protocol Pass unlocks the [Basic Supply] tier by default.
The [Protocol Customized] tier can be purchased, while the [Originium Supply] tier can be unlocked by spending [Origeometry].

<@intru.bold>- Protocol Pass EXP and Levels -</>
There are 2 major ways to earn Protocol Pass EXP, which then levels up the Protocol Pass and grants you rewards.
· Complete Pass Missions (some missions will become available after meeting certain criteria).
· Take part in [Operational Manual - Daily Tasks] and claim the max daily Activity Points rewards.
※ If max Activity Points is not reached for the day, 1 Vacation Tag will be activated at 04:00 (Server Time) of the following day. Up to 3 tags can be activated.
※ After earning max Activity Points and claiming the rewards, 1 activated Vacation Tag will be consumed to give double Pass EXP (Daily task rewards are not affected by this).

Even after maxing the seasonal Protocol Pass level, you can still earn Pass EXP with the aforementioned methods and acquire cyclical rewards. There is no limit to earning Pass EXP that exceed the level cap.

※ Special EXP bonus details: Unlocking [Originium Supply] / [Protocol Customized] tiers of the seasonal Protocol Pass grants +3% / +3% Pass EXP bonus respectively, for a total of +6% Pass EXP bonus when both tiers are unlocked.

<@intru.bold>- Protocol Pass Missions Details -</>
· Weekly Missions: During the Protocol Pass season, weekly missions become available every 7 days. Weekly missions will be reset when the pass season ends.
· Horizons Missions: These are a special type of Protocol Pass missions that are permanently available. Horizons Missions progress will not be reset when the pass season ends, meaning that these missions can be performed during any pass season to claim their rewards. When all Horizons Missions are completed, its special screen will be closed at 04:00 (server time) of the following day.

<@intru.bold>- Protocol Pass Weapons Details -</>
For each pass season, the [Originium Supply] and [Protocol Customized] tiers each contain a special weapon supply.
Every pass season has its own weapon supplies. In other words, weapon supplies from a current season may give a list of weapon choices that differ from those of previous seasons. Also, lists of weapon choices from seasons already released will not change.
[Protocolized Weapon Patterns] can raise the potential of any weapon provided by Protocol Pass weapon supplies, including weapon supplies from future pass seasons.

<@intru.bold>- Special Rules -</>
When the Protocol Pass season ends, any unclaimed pass level rewards shall be sent to your Inbox.
For excessive purchases of [Protocol Customized] due to special circumstances, rewards from [Protocol Customized] tier will not stack. Instead, an amount of [Origeometry] based on the value of the purchase will be returned to you.

<@intru.bold>- Exchange Crate-o-Surprise Details -</>
[Exchange Crates-o-Surprise] are automatically opened when acquired. Crate contents are fixed: a random Oroberyl reward and a random progression material reward.

<@profile.key>I still remember the first time I met Ekut. The patrolling Huntsingers brought her back to the camp and the girl was barely alive. It was difficult for us to fathom why such a young child was left to roam the wildlands for months on her own, a suffering that almost killed her with malnutrition and thirst. To treat the injuries on her right arm, we were forced to reconnect the nerves with circuitry. Of course, there is no need to be worried about the hazards posed by her right hand. We have designed a special pair of insulation gloves so that she may live normally like us. 
I named her Ekut, based on the strong and intelligent burdenbeast of our hanna. It is my hope that she could grow up strong, and survive the wind and frost like the powerful burdenbeast. She achieved all that, and went beyond my expectations. 
But Ekut grew up with an immense duty that seemed far too heavy for her. Perhaps it was her early victory over death itself, or her powerful name we took from the hanna. When she turned fifteen, Ekut started to seek the songs and roamed the wildlands. The Songseeker did everything she could to help villages and towns in dire straits, even when the challenges were far too great. 
I still remember that rainstorm. During our rescue operation, Ekut ventured alone into the heart of the tempest. We thought she would never come back. Just when all hopes seemed lost, an arc of lightning streaked across the sky. Like that arc, she pierced the fury of nature and leaped onto the last wagon. And with this act, the wildlands began to address her as Arclight. The name was woven into the hanna of numerous Songseekers. She took a name from the verses and returned a new name to their songs. 
I was not surprised when Arclight told me that she wanted to seek new answers from Endfield. In fact, it reminded me of the choice I made when I was younger. I once roamed far to the canopies of starry night, and from there I felt a chorus of hope and courage assembled in the floating city. 
Those memories felt like they belonged to a lifetime ago. But I believe that as long as the stars still shine in the sky, Civilization will one day be united once more. I also believe that Arclight, along with the names and oaths she wove into her hanna, will find the answers she truly seeks. 
— Letter of Recommendation for Endfield Industries, written by Aldertone Orisha</>

<@profile.key>TRAINING LOG I 
ENVIRONMENT: Setting C 
GRAVITY: Setting 2 
SUBJECT: Gilberta 
RECORDER: Lil' Dodge 
Gilberta's training performance exceeded all benchmarks. For her Arts specialization, we modified the chamber with gravity field generators and tactical release nodes, anticipating a lengthy adjustment period. Yet her combat instincts proved sharper than projected: mission accomplished in 1/3 the estimated time, with notably restrained collateral damage (a rarity for these fragile systems, as you know). Her gravitational control hints at paradigm-shifting potential: a tactician who warps the battlefield itself, or perhaps a one-woman armada-breaker. With this being said, I'm sure every commander will vie for her deployment. 
Our next step is clear: help Gilberta unlock her full potential and refine her tactical instincts. Her abilities can turn the tide under any condition — and that's thrilling. 

TRAINING LOG VI 
ENVIRONMENT: Setting S
GRAVITY: Setting 26 
SUBJECT: Gilberta 
RECORDER: Lil' Dodge 
In recent training sessions, we've been exploring Gilberta's control over her Arts. When we increased the number of non-directional gravity sources to eight, her control over the surrounding field showed a marked decline. Most of the time, she was able to maintain stable gravity around herself, but at critical environmental thresholds, she could no longer stabilize areas a few meters away — which means she couldn't ensure the safety of nearby teammates. 
All relevant parameters and environmental conditions have been uploaded to EFDB. While Talos-II is unlikely to present situations with multiple gravity sources shifting unpredictably, the risks our operators face extend beyond this planet. At certain Depths, any battlefield condition is possible. 
Gilberta expressed some dissatisfaction with her performance, but she did more than enough. This training was designed specifically to test the limits of her abilities — and it's now our task to develop the next training phase accordingly.</>

5201204394807128073:
Interested in the story of the messenger named Falken Gravning?
Hardly any Terran remembered his name. What they did remember was his job — a Catastrophe Messenger.
Falken was born in the borders of Kazimierz and started this lonesome career when he was but a young man. With sturdy steps he hiked across mountains and navigated rivers to bring verified data of Catastrophe signs to villages, towns, and cities facing inevitable destruction. He was not a savior. The only thing he could do was to warn people of the "impending footsteps of annihilation". Some were grateful, while others bore grudges. He suffered more than a few wounds, vile curses, as well as cold, hateful gaze over the years, and witnessed grave sacrifices as well. Suffocating depression constantly loomed over his soul.
When he turned 53, he decided to leave his homeland behind and devote the final years of his life to the newly discovered planet — Talos-II.
Here in the new world, he was no longer a "prophet of doom" but a mere common messenger. For those few short years, the serene, open expanses of Talos-II was free from Catastrophes and the ever-present threat of destruction. A sense of long-absent peace filled Falken. He took his backpack and roamed the lands between the pioneering bases, delivering letters, escorting supplies, and conveying intel with every trip.
When he had time for himself, he continued to travel alone. He even cobbled together several Originium devices to create a rudimentary aircraft. Though it flew awkwardly across the skies, he could land it upon unexplored wilderness. He climbed majestic peaks, waded through dark swamps, and left his footprints in this untouched realm.
He started to picture a beautiful future for the land untouched by Catastrophes — Once he retires, he would build a wooden cabin in some valley. He would also have a mountaintop summer retreat where he could enjoy clean, refreshing air. His notebook was filled with trails, routes, contour maps, and ideas for his "ideal home". As he spread footprints across the world, more and more of the blank areas were filled.
Until that very day.
The day when the Ankhors fell from the skies and the Aggeloi descended upon Civilization. People were once again forced to flee as they had done with Catastrophes struck.
During the era of chaos, Falken once again took up his old profession. He became the most reliable guide and led the survivors in a desperate southbound trek of survival. People said he stepped up to the challenge in numerous occasions to mark out the road forward. He even flew that ramshackle aircraft of his into the storm, and returned with a beaten and badly wounded body. With experience, grit, and courage, he paved multiple trails of life for the refugees. Numerous outposts, villages, and towns were founded thanks to his way markers or verbal directions. Without Falken as their guide, many would fail to reach the Civilization Band alive.
But that was not the end of Falken's journey.
During the last years of his life, Falken continued to journey south. He traversed the mountain ranges and roamed the entire Band until he finally arrived at the edge of the great ocean. Legend then claimed that Falken built a ship at that very place and sailed off to find a place even further south.
And Falken was never seen again after that.
A particular story was rather popular amongst the oceanic navigators of Talos-II: Should one see a cloud, shaped like a raised mast with full sails at the place where the oceans and heavens meet, that would be "Falken's Sail", and that would be tidings for good weather.
People call him the "Navigator". Falken's story was told in every city, school, and port. He was a messenger, a pathfinder, a lonely traveler, and the one who raised the beacon high during humanity's hour of darkness.
Mieszko Industries is proud to uphold this concept. Our latest series for this year have been imbued with the spirit of the Navigator. We dedicate it to every ambitious and courageous individual eager to face the boundless future.

"This is just a promotional tale. Is this all I'm going to read?"
"Of course not. I'm about to introduce this latest paper on the untold secrets of Falken Gravning."
"Oh?"
"Falken Gravning kept going south because of his belief that another undiscovered Cosmic Gate may exist in the south pole of this world."
"Another ... Cosmic Gate? Is that even possible?"
"Who knows? Nobody could prove nor disprove it. Who knows? He might have found a way home at the end of the sea, or simply disappeared beneath the waves."
"So..."
"So towards the end of his life, what kept the 'Navigator' going wasn't his passion for exploration or adventure. It was a far more deeper desire — He wanted to go home."

......
Theoretically speaking, the yield was ... feasible. My calculations placed it within achievable limits but the numbers look risky. I had to redesign the structure of the Arts Unit but this would ... double the weight of the entire setup.
......
A powered eviscerator with a moving chain of cutting bits? Their demands are getting nuttier with every single day. Are they really going to smash an enemy's head with this Arts Unit? Come to think about it, the current build does have enough room for a motor. Maybe I'll give it a shot.
......

......
It was a monumental sight that I'd remember for life. The Aggelos was as big as a mountain and its carcass blocked the entire valley. <@profile.key>In the beginning, children at the Den of the Brave always poked fun at Adelheid. No one really knew the girl who lived so far away. She was shy, introverted, dressed in boring clothing, slow to react, and never caught the ball during conversations. "Biggie" Tom started by badmouthing her at every turn. He wanted her out of the children's secret base. But Tom eventually relented because of two reasons: The grown-ups respected the Caprinae couple who adopted Adelheid, and even though she was teary eyed and sniveling, she never forgot about stuffing herself with apple peelings and turnip leaves. 

Everything changed in that atrocious summer. The rains poured in June, the entire place was flooded, and the bandits were finally evicted after a grueling battle. The ordeal left scars upon five families who lost their loved ones. The unsuspecting children followed the procession to the suburbs, and they saw her atop the hills. Adelheid, except it was not the little crybaby they knew. They saw the girl and her family cleaning out the resting places, cleaning the headstones, and offering elegies to the deceased. It was not until the coffin was laid to rest when the children finally realized that Tom would no longer return to Den of the Brave. 
Instead of fear, it was panic and denial that spread. The children could not accept the machinations of fate, and failed to figure out a way to make up for the missing position. It was then when Adelheid placed a simple wooden statuette before Tom's grave. It was very roughly carved, crooked, imbalanced, and unpolished. 
"He always wanted a figurine of a Competition Knight," the girl said. "That would be Tom's final wish." 
The grown-ups fail to control their tears again. They lamented the death of a life so innocent and young. 
But the children tried not to laugh as the statuette looked nothing like a Competition Knight. 
In the end, they bore it no longer and burst out laughing. 
They took out their Knight Cards and discussed how to make the statuette more knight-like. Although Adelheid failed to follow their conversation and the task of carving the figurine fell to a more dexterous companion, the children would always hand the new and much improved statuette into Adelheid's hands, for she was tasked with leading their own procession into the cemetery and perform the annual ceremony. 
"Tom is right here," the girl promised every year. 
No one knew how Adelheid was so certain about this, or how she learned of Tom's wishes. Nobody seemed to care about how she performed her work. 

In the end, Adelheid did not break her shell. She remained rather inept at expressing herself. Every time her tummy rumbled, she became so embarrassed she would start inching to a nearby dustbin. But whenever new kids arrive in town and start talking about the strange girl humming songs in the bushes, someone would tap them on the shoulder and give them a quite a story.</>

5762123140210423383:
The man walked in and quickly slammed the door of the simple barracks. The recalcitrant door barely managed a painful creak before it was forcibly shut to block the frigid air outside. The man then looked around and breathed a long sigh of relief. His daughter was still asleep in her cubicle. The cub of the Pack was four, and the hardest to coddle to sleep.
His wife prepared the weapons. The scope and Arts Unit had been taken apart, the parts laid out across the table. She was wholly focused on honing a short blade when her man walked in.
"Cleaning up the weapons rack?" The man sat on the opposite side of the table and pried open a preheated tin of meat provisions. The temperature was just right and appetizing enough.
"I hardly make the wrong guesses, dear. You'll be using these soon enough, right?"
"I actually wanted to play a prank on you and tell you that: 'My sweet darling, your judgment about the Hunt Meet was completely off.' Unfortunately, the Old Wolves said those very same words, as though they read a secret script you prepared for them... So yes, I lost the bet and so I'll coddle our pup to sleep for a week... But just so you know, I don't like losing."
The woman threw the sharpened blade to her man and gestured him to try the balance. She then picked up a gun to load it up with ammo.
"The Pack never shared Jakub's views. The Landbreaker clans will definitely break apart... And if we're no longer 'friends', we can only be this — predator and prey... The clan must hunt them down and feast upon the kill. We'll become clannibals."
"Clannibals... I like that word. Old Louis shared that view in the meeting: 'The Civilization Band is closing its grip around the Landbreakers' neck. The Wolves cannot die like this. We must see if our friends are good enough for the table...' Hah! That old geezer has a way with words."
"So which Clan will it be?"
"Bonekrushers. They like Jakub too much. These fanatics kinda disgust me."
"And the hit?"
"A denstack smash-and-run, maybe? Grab their supplies tonight and then head home right afterwards. Nobody would know that the Pack did it. If I set off in half an hour, I can even make it back for breakfast."
"Just don't forget to say goodbye to our baby."
"...We probably shouldn't wake her."
"You sure?"
"I'm sure. The hit is just a stroll in the park..."
*BAMMM*.
The man saw his woman slam the gun on the table and coldly glared at him. An unloaded bullet rolled across the table, fell off the corner, clinked on the floor, and continued its journey to the corner of the barracks. He knew his wife saw through his lies.
"Don't lie to me."
"I never..."
"Guessing the details of your meeting wasn't hard... Jakub's negotiations with the Civilization Band fell apart. He and his loyalists will be torn apart... There's only one thing you want ... to keep the Pack safe in these turbulent times." The woman paused and breathed deeply before continuing. "Wolves will be killing Wolves. The Clan will be forced to do housekeeping. Those who stand with Jakub will be eliminated. Even the Wolves who made their 'names' in the Civilization Band by raiding and killing will be bled dry and left to die in the wildlands. And that isn't the end of it. Some of you will be sent out to war with the other Clans. Direct, open war. It's a sign. The Banders know the best time for their offensive approaches. They know the Pack takes a different path compared to the other Clans... You want to rush the end of the Landbreakers... And some of you volunteered for this suicidal path so that the Clan can survive."
"How did you guess?"
"Because my tally is higher than yours, dear. I see murder glistening in your eyes."
"Love, I do not fear this... Maybe when I close my eyes, I'll see Nonno waiting at our old villa in Siracusa... I'll tell him that I took care of my beloved wife, my baby girl, and all the other cubs... I'll tell him that our legacy lives on, running atop the grazing fields, counting creds in a city alley, or even embracing new lives as Talosians... Our Famiglia name will be cleansed anew with the name of our Clan... No matter the life we chose... the Pack will decide for ourselves..."
"I'll go with you."
"I forbid it. I chose to join this Hunt and accept death so that you may live. And you must live, even if you have to forget about our homes and abandon the Famiglia. I..."
The man could not go on. The girl's little palm opened to reveal the bullet that rolled off to the corner.
"Good hunting, Papa..."
His girl just woke up and heard only part of the conversation, but that was enough. He originally planned to leave without goodbye, and had to armor his resolve by taking a long walk in the blistering cold. But those soft words of encouragement shattered it and jerked him out from the great river called Death.
"I..."
"We are bound by blood, and that is how legacy is carried out, isn't it?"
The soft hands, small hands, and rough hands gripped each other.
"Before the cubs could freely roam the wilderness, no one can kill us. No one."

5931956550209320020: <@profile.key>Seven years ago, during the autumn when I left Juniper Security, I worked as a part-time instructor at a youth training camp somewhere close to home. I was hoping to take care of my sick father and make some money for his treatment. My main job description was to share various tidbits about military basics with children who had probably never set foot in the Band Fringes. I worked in the youth camp for three years, and a 15-year old student named Ruy left quite an impression on me. He was the only one in the cohort who signed up temporarily. They told me his parents did not want him to join, but conceded upon the boy's strong insistence. I often reflect upon this moment and think I should have taken this as a warning sign for things to come. Despite being so thin that he looked malnourished, Ruy was not as obedient as he appeared. Ruy only attended eleven courses throughout the entire term, and he "found problems" in eight of them. These problems ranged from slight deviations from textbook examples of military poise to one or two minor memory slips. In fact, he pointed out any non-conformances in my course that could be considered errors. Things escalated to the point where I had to rehearse my materials before every class just so the boy wouldn't call out my mistakes. On the eve of graduation, I finally eased off my usual sternness as an instructor and asked the boy a question that had troubled me for months, "I need to know why you're so obsessed about finding your instructor's mistakes? Did I make you angry at some point?" I still remember the expression on his face. He shook his head, and then took out a copy of How to Be a Proper Soldier? (Young Adults Edition) published by the TGCC. The manual was flipped through so many times that the corners curled. Then he pointed the book at me and gave me a serious look. "No, Instructor Luca. Your classes were very interesting, and your examples made things way more engaging than the manual. I actually liked your lessons a lot... But you probably didn't know that everything in this manual was the only fount of strength that's kept me this far." "I ... I really care about every pointer in the manual because I want to put them to use on a real battlefield... I've been dreaming about this since I was nine..." After hearing these words, I finally learned about Ruy's childhood from another instructor and a close friend of mine — turned out that young Ruy contracted Oripathy due to momentary familial negligence. Though timely treatment was provided, the poor lad was almost forced to live out the rest of his life on a sickbed. I do not know what he experienced or sacrificed in order to receive training like the other students... But as his instructor, I do approve of his efforts and proudly call him a student of mine, despite the fact that many of his actions had caused no small trouble on my part. Come to think of it, if not for Ruy's constant, incessant, and persistent corrections, I would never have worked so hard to ensure conformance to the training materials. I probably would never correct my habits of mindless and rote memorization back in the force. And I most certainly would never have made it into the elite armed security training program or become an formal instructor for a mercenary outfit. ............ After my father passed away, I left Alloycarrot and drifted away from my training camp colleagues... I did not know where Ruy went afterwards. An accidental encounter with a former student of mine informed me that Ruy seemed to have joined a relatively famous company as part of their security detail... Truth be told, I was a little surprised. I thought that boy would have become an officer or instructor... Regardless, I sincerely hope he will make good use of the knowledge he acquired and fulfill his childhood dreams. — An excerpt from Those Not Remembered, an autobiography by the legendary instructor Luca Londi

The judges and other tasters of this dish have arrived at a unanimous conclusion: The chef who prepared this plate of bamboo sprouts and meat knew perfect heat control! The young bamboo sprouts were sweet and crunchy, while the fillet slices were juicy and tender. Quick stir-frying over strong fire perfectly combined the two. The sprouts soaked up the rich gravy as the fillet slices absorbed the refreshing aromas of the bamboo grove.
But everything after the stir-frying revealed the chef's shortcomings. Too many condiments were used. The aroma of redjade ginseng also overpowered the flavors of the primary ingredients. The judges really had to work their palates to peel away the distractions before finally arriving at the refreshing tastes of nature and cozy family stoves. In conclusion, this dish felt like a dime a dozen.

ABSTRACT: This investigation specifically focuses on the automation of Xiranite machinery and discusses potential possibilities and concepts for jointly applying said machinery in the Automated Industry Complex. This paper explores actual scenarios and applications for inter-disciplinary and multi-sector efforts for integrated Blight containment and remediation, and summarizes methodologies that improves safety guarantees as well as the efficiency of coordinated operations. ............

"The paper... Argh. Don't flatter me, Endmin. I'll get really embarrassed. It's just based on the basic theories you came up with years ago. This is far from a breakthrough." 
"..."

"..." 
"Mountains would only get higher, so the highest peak is always beyond reach? Ohoho. I admire your confidence! But the more you say it, the greater my urge to challenge the hike. By the way, I've been looking up about your Automated Industry Complex and worked out a brand new tech. It's something you never wrote about..." 
"..." 
"I'm definitely not your match. I call this joint growth through competition! If you want me to be honest with you, it's because ... your AIC Factory is terrific. I like this tech. From the bottom of my heart. If only we had this tech back then... If I could get this AIC when I was twenty..." 
"..." 
"You're right. It's never too late...!" </>
